   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2024/3214 of 16 October 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2015/757 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the rules for the monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions from offshore ships and the zero-rating of sustainable fuels», a European Union instrument that changes how greenhouse gas emissions from certain ships are counted and reported. Its reach is stated in the text: «Greenhouse gas emissions from offshore ships shall cover greenhouse gas emissions released during voyages from last port of call to a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State to next port of call, as well as within ports of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State». It was published in the Official Journal on «L series 2024/3214 27.12.2024». What the Regulation says is quoted from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*; points for counsel are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation amends the European Union's ship-emissions monitoring rules (the MRV Regulation). It changes them in two ways. First, it says which ships count as offshore ships, listing among others: «(a) anchor handling tug supply vessel; (b) offshore supply ship; (c) crew/supply vessel; (d) pipe carrier; (e) platform supply ship; (f) drilling ship;» and at the end of the list «(ad) dredger; (ae) hopper dredger.» The 2023 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/957 is the source of the inclusion: «notably to provide for the inclusion of greenhouse gas emissions from offshore ships within the scope of that Regulation from 1 January 2025». The reason for the list is given in the recitals: «clarifying the term ‘offshore ships’ is necessary to ensure a uniform application with regards to the determination of the greenhouse gas emissions covered by the Regulation».

Second, it changes how emissions from sustainable fuels are counted: «By way of derogation from point 1.1, companies shall not apply the rules laid down in Part A of Annex I to this Regulation as regards the determination of the CO 2 emission factors where the company uses Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin (RFNBO), Recycled Carbon Fuel (RCF) or synthetic low-carbon fuel.» The derogation has an earlier start: «However, Article 1, point (2), shall apply from 1 January 2024.» For those fuels «the CO 2 emission factor shall be determined in accordance with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066.»

The Regulation takes effect as follows: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». It is «binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation addresses shipping companies and their ships, and a forwarder is not named. A freight business that books cargo or services on a ship of one of the listed types is dealing with a ship that falls under these monitoring rules; the text does not say who bears any resulting cost. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular fuel qualifies as one of the fuels named in the derogation.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: from 1 January 2027 offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above enter the EU Emissions Trading System, a cost the texts place on the shipping company. No step falls on a business that is not a shipping company within the next 30 days, but two dated events are close. The Regulation «It shall apply from 1 January 2025.» and the next dated step is in the recitals: «no later than 31 December 2026, the Commission should present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council» on whether smaller offshore ships should be added to the EU Emissions Trading System. For offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above the system starts next year: «From 1 January 2027, offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above are included in the scope of maritime transport activities covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council».

- A carrier-relations lead lists, before the Commission report is due, which ships on current bookings are of the types named in the Regulation's list, and asks each shipping company whether its monitoring plan is submitted and whether the ship carries a Document of Compliance.
- A pricing lead asks the owners of those ships, before the start of 2027 quotes, whether an allowance charge will be added once the ship enters the EU Emissions Trading System.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the dates quoted above; the Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any cost reaching the shipping company under these rules can be charged on to a forwarder or its client under the contracts the business holds.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation's duties sit with the company responsible for the ship. In the guidance of ABS (American Bureau of Shipping), «the shipping company must submit the monitoring plan of the offshore ship to its administering authority within three months after the ship’s first port of call in a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State.» The European Maritime Safety Agency adds that «Each company is associated with the administering authority of one Member State.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder is not named in these texts; it meets the Regulation through the shipping company whose ship carries its cargo. *Industry interpretation:* the guidance quoted is ABS's reading of the MRV rules, not the Regulation's own text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party is the company responsible for a given ship on a given booking.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Commission publishes general guidance for shipping companies. Its cover reads: «The EU ETS and MRV Maritime General guidance for shipping companies» with the version line «Guidance Document No. 1, Updated Version, 18 November 2025.»

*Analytical inference:* the guidance is the Commission's own reading of the MRV and EU Emissions Trading System rules for ships; the stored text holds only its cover and version line, so no section-by-section reading is made here. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which sections of the guidance apply to a given offshore ship.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The recitals set a Commission report: «in which it should examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in that Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage.» The report «may be accompanied, if appropriate, by legislative proposals».

The Commission's shipping page dates the system's start for large ships: «Since January 2024, the EU's Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) has been extended to cover CO 2 emissions from all large ships». It also records a wider proposal: «On 17 July 2026, the European Commission proposed a targeted revision of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)» which «strengthens the existing ETS for aviation and maritime transport».

*Analytical inference:* the report of 31 December 2026 and the July 2026 proposal are the points where the ship sizes and rules in this Regulation could change; the stored text does not say whether the proposal alters the offshore-ship list. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission report or the proposal changes which offshore ships a business deals with.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the texts held pose no disputed threshold question beyond the ship list in section 2.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope of the monitoring. The Regulation's own list of offshore ships excludes one class: «by the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations». Offshore ships fell under the MRV Regulation from: «from 1 January 2025, general cargo ships between 400 and 5000 gross tonnage, and offshore ships of 400 gross tonnage and above, fell under the scope of the amended MRV Regulation».

Reports and plans. «From 2025, by 31 March of each year, companies must, for each ship under their responsibility , submit an emissions report for the entire reporting period of the previous year, which has been verified as satisfactory by a verifier in accordance with Article 13 of the MRV Regulation». A ship also carries a certificate: «Document of compliance: by 30 June of each year, companies must ensure that all their ships that have performed activities in the previous reporting period and are visiting ports in the European Economic Area carry on board a document of compliance. This might be subject to inspections by Member States' authorities.»

Emissions Trading System. The Emissions Trading System Directive was amended by Directive (EU) 2023/959; ABS reads it for offshore ships as: «Directive (EU) 2023/959 amending Directive 2003/87/EC provides that, regarding an offshore ship, a “port of call” includes the port where the ship stops to relieve the crew.» ABS reads the start for large offshore ships as: «Beginning 1 January 2027, the EU ETS Directive will be expanded to cover offshore vessels exceeding 5,000 GT, which will be required to surrender allowances at company level by 30 September 2028.» The Commission's page describes how surrender is phased for ships in the system: «shipping companies only have to surrender allowances for a portion of their emissions during an initial phase-in period: 2025: for 40% of their emissions reported in 2024; 2026: for 70% of their emissions reported in 2025; 2027 onwards: for 100% of their reported emissions.»

Penalty. No penalty: the text of this Regulation states no penalty, fine or enforcement consequence.

*Analytical inference:* the duties in this section fall on shipping companies; the phase-in quoted is the Commission's description for ships in the system generally, and the text does not say it applies to offshore ships. *Industry interpretation:* the 30 September 2028 surrender date is ABS's reading. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of these duties reach a forwarder, and whether the phase-in applies to offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 7.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets monitoring rules for ships, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reports go through a central system: «The emissions report must be submitted through THETIS-MRV to:» the administering authority, the flag State authorities where the flag is an EEA country, and the European Commission. From the 2025 reporting year the report also goes to the administering authority: «As from 31 March 2025, emissions reports should also be submitted to the responsible administering authority trough THETIS-MRV.» The ABS list of steps for offshore ships gives «By 31 March 2026 and each year, submit to the responsible administering authority, to the ship’s flag State (for ships flying the flag of a Member State) and to the EU Commission a verified emissions report for the entire reporting period of the previous year.» and «By 30 June 2026 and each year, carry onboard a valid Document of Compliance (DoC).» The monitoring plan has a separate route, and for offshore ships outside the Emissions Trading System «there is no requirement for approval by the administering authority (only submission).»

*Analytical inference:* these registration and report duties fall on the company responsible for the ship; the texts state none on a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client or shipping company may ask a forwarder for voyage data.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the system work sits with shipping companies, and it has a start date. ABS lists the first steps: «From 1 January 2025, start monitoring CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions and activity data according to the verified EU MRV monitoring plan for the offshore ships with a port of call in a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State.» Later: «By 31 March 2028 and each year, companies shall submit to the administering authority for offshore ships of 5000 GT and above an aggregated report at company level for the emissions of the previous calendar year.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder that books offshore ships sees this as the ship owner's data and reporting work, not as a system to build; the texts state no data request to forwarders. *Industry interpretation:* the action list is ABS's. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a shipping company may ask a forwarder for voyage data.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

«Ships operated in stationary mode still fall within the scope of EU ETS but for stationary installations.» ABS adds that «such ships will not be subject to other obligations as set in the MRV Maritime Regulation, such as reporting emissions within a port of call, as long as they remain stationary.»

*Industry interpretation:* this is ABS's reading. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular offshore ship counts as operated in stationary mode.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no adjacent industry research or alternative is held for this Regulation.*

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1 January 2024: Article 1, point (2), the sustainable-fuel emission factor rule, applies (in force)
- 16 October 2024: the Commission adopted this Regulation (in force on its third day after publication)
- 1 January 2025: the Regulation applies; offshore ships of 400 gross tonnage and above fall under the MRV Regulation (in force)
- 31 March 2025: under the MRV Regulation, emissions reports also go to the administering authority (past)
- 31 March 2026: under the MRV Regulation, verified emissions report due for offshore ships (past)
- 30 June 2026: under the MRV Regulation, Document of Compliance carried on board (past)
- 31 December 2026: Commission report on smaller offshore ships due
- 1 January 2027: offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above included in the EU Emissions Trading System
- 31 March 2028: under the EU Emissions Trading System, company-level report due for offshore ships of 5000 GT and above
- 30 September 2028: surrender date for allowances at company level, as read by ABS

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2019/943 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 5 June 2019 on the internal market for electricity (recast)», the European Union rulebook for how electricity is traded, priced and moved across borders. Its aim is stated in Article 1: «set the basis for an efficient achievement of the objectives of the Energy Union and in particular the climate and energy framework for 2030 by enabling market signals to be delivered for increased efficiency, higher share of renewable energy sources, security of supply, flexibility, sustainability, decarbonisation and innovation». Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» The text is marked «(Text with EEA relevance)». It was adopted as «Done at Brussels, 5 June 2019.» What the Regulation says is quoted from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*; points for counsel are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation replaces the earlier electricity trading rules («Regulation (EC) No 714/2009 is repealed.») and sets the rules of the internal market: «This Regulation establishes rules to ensure the functioning of the internal market for electricity and includes requirements related to the development of renewable forms of energy and environmental policy». Its recitals say who the system is for: «The Energy Union aims to provide final customers – household and business – with safe, secure, sustainable, competitive and affordable energy.»

It takes effect as follows: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union», and «It shall apply from 1 January 2020.» Some articles start earlier: «Notwithstanding the first subparagraph, Articles 14, 15, 22(4), 23(3) and (6), 35, 36 and 62 shall apply from the date of entry into force of this Regulation.»

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation addresses network operators, power exchanges, regulators and Member States. A freight business meets it as a buyer of electricity, which the Regulation counts as a market participant, and as a final customer for tariffs; the Regulation does not mention freight, transport operators or logistics sites.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days, but the rules behind its electricity bill have a dated review ahead. The nearest is «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall, where appropriate, submit legislative proposals on the basis of its assessment.» On price, the text states «There shall be neither a maximum nor a minimum limit to the wholesale electricity price.» On network charges it states «Those charges shall not include unrelated costs supporting unrelated policy objectives.»

- A procurement lead asks each electricity supplier, at the next contract renewal, how wholesale price movements and network charges are passed into the price paid, and records whether the contract sets a cap or floor.
- A regulatory-affairs lead reads the Commission legislative proposals once published after 31 December 2026 for changes to the price and network-charge articles, and notes which change the electricity line of the budget.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the quoted articles; the Regulation states no pass-through of wholesale prices or network charges to a final customer's contract, so the first step is a question to the supplier, not a finding. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a final customer or a market participant for each of its sites.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation's duties sit with transmission system operators, power exchanges (NEMOs), regulators and Member States: «Transmission system operators shall not take any measures for the purpose of changing wholesale prices.» For a customer, the term used is «‘final customer’ means final customer as defined in point (3) of Article 2 of Directive (EU) 2019/944». Market participants carry one duty directly: «All market participants shall be responsible for the imbalances they cause in the system». Tariffs reach customers as the text says: «Where appropriate, the level of the tariffs applied to producers or final customers, or both shall provide locational signals at Union level».

The Regulation defines who a market participant is: «‘market participant’ means a natural or legal person who buys, sells or generates electricity, who is engaged in aggregation or who is an operator of demand response or energy storage services». The duty then follows: «market participants shall either be balance responsible parties or shall contractually delegate their responsibility to a balance responsible party of their choice».

*Analytical inference:* on these words a business that buys electricity falls within the definition of a market participant, so Article 5(1) reaches it, directly or through a balance responsible party it delegates to; the text also uses the separate term final customer for tariffs. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that only buys electricity is a market participant for each site, which duties follow, and how its supply contract handles balance responsibility.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance document on this Regulation is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation sets its own review steps. «By 1 July 2025, the Commission shall review the existing network codes and guidelines in order to assess which of their provisions could be appropriately incorporated into legislative acts of the Union concerning the internal electricity market» That date has passed; the text held does not say what the review found. Next: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall, where appropriate, submit legislative proposals on the basis of its assessment.» Regulators have a later report: «By 1 January 2028, regulatory authorities shall report to the Commission and ACER on the share of the total capacity covered by contracts with a duration or a procurement period of longer than one day.» In the balancing market article, a contract-length limit starts in 2026: «Notwithstanding paragraph 10, from 1 January 2026 contract periods shall not be longer than six months.» The full review is set for the end of the decade: «By 31 December 2030 the Commission shall review this Regulation and shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the basis of that review, accompanied by a legislative proposal where appropriate.»

*Analytical inference:* the 31 December 2026 proposals are the first point at which the price and network-charge articles could change; the Regulation does not say they will. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether proposals published after that date alter any article a business relies on.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the texts held pose no disputed threshold question for a freight business beyond the role question in section 4.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. Article 1, headed subject matter and scope, states the Regulation's aim: «Article 1 Subject matter and scope This Regulation aims to:» and its first aim is to «set the basis for an efficient achievement of the objectives of the Energy Union and in particular the climate and energy framework for 2030». The rules apply to market participants as defined in section 4, to network operators, exchanges, regulators and Member States as the articles below say.

Price formation. «There shall be neither a maximum nor a minimum limit to the wholesale electricity price.» NEMOs may still apply harmonised limits for day-ahead and intraday trading: «NEMOs may apply harmonised limits on maximum and minimum clearing prices for day-ahead and intraday timeframes.»

Imbalance settlement. «By 1 January 2021, the imbalance settlement period shall be 15 minutes in all scheduling areas, unless regulatory authorities have granted a derogation or an exemption.» Then: «From 1 January 2025, the imbalance settlement period shall not exceed 30 minutes where an exemption has been granted by all the regulatory authorities within a synchronous area.»

Cross-border capacity. «for borders using a coordinated net transmission capacity approach, the minimum capacity shall be 70 % of the transmission capacity respecting operational security limits after deduction of contingencies», and «That minimum capacity shall be reached by 31 December 2025.»

Network charges. «Those charges shall not be distance-related.»

Capacity mechanisms. «(a) from 4 July 2019 at the latest, generation capacity that started commercial production on or after that date and that emits more than 550 g of CO 2 of fossil fuel origin per kWh of electricity shall not be committed or to receive payments or commitments for future payments under a capacity mechanism;» «(b) from 1 July 2025 at the latest, generation capacity that started commercial production before 4 July 2019 and that emits more than 550 g of CO 2 of fossil fuel origin per kWh of electricity and more than 350 kg CO 2 of fossil fuel origin on average per year per installed kWe shall not be committed or receive payments or commitments for future payments under a capacity mechanism.»

Penalties. «the Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation, the network codes adopted pursuant to Article 59, and the guidelines adopted pursuant to Article 61» The Commission side: «The Commission may, by decision, impose on undertakings fines not exceeding 1 % of the total turnover in the preceding business year where, intentionally or negligently, those undertakings supply incorrect, incomplete or misleading information».

*Analytical inference:* these duties fall mainly on network operators, power exchanges, regulators and generators; the balance-responsibility duty in section 4 reaches every market participant, and a business that buys electricity falls within that definition. The quoted articles state no pass-through of the capacity limits or charges into a customer's price. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that only buys electricity is a market participant, which of these duties reach it, and which reach a business that also generates or stores electricity on site.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 13.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets rules for the electricity market, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties sit with Member States, network operators and regulators, and most dates have passed. «Member States shall provide a report to the Commission by 5 January 2020 detailing the measures and actions they have taken or intend to take.» «By 5 October 2019 all relevant transmission system operators shall submit a proposal for the methodology and assumptions that are to be used in the bidding zone review process». «By 5 July 2020 the ENTSO for Electricity shall submit to ACER:» a methodology set out in the article, and «By 5 July 2021 the ENTSO for Electricity shall set up and operate the registry» for capacity providers.

*Analytical inference:* the dated reports above fall on Member States, network operators and ENTSO for Electricity, and the dates are past; the articles quoted here state no separate registration duty on a market participant, but Article 5(1) requires market participants to be balance responsible parties or to delegate that role by contract. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that only buys electricity, or one with on-site generation or storage, has a registration or contract duty.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the system work sits with network operators and exchanges, and one article opens the market to customers. «NEMOs shall provide products for trading in day-ahead and intraday markets which are sufficiently small in size, with minimum bid sizes of 500 kW or less, to allow for the effective participation of demand-side response, energy storage and small-scale renewables including direct participation by customers.» Regional coordination also had a start date: «shall enter into operation by 1 July 2022».

*Analytical inference:* a freight site with its own storage or flexible load could use the small bid sizes; the text says nothing about freight sites, so the step for a site manager is to ask the supplier or an aggregator whether a bid of that size is open to the site. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a site may take part directly or only through a supplier or aggregator.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Regulation lets Member States and regulators depart from some rules. Balance responsibility: «Member States may provide derogations from balance responsibility only for:» among them «installations benefitting from support approved by the Commission under Union State aid rules pursuant to Articles 107, 108 and 109 TFEU, and commissioned before 4 July 2019». The exemption narrows over time: «For power-generating facilities commissioned from 1 January 2026, point (b) of paragraph 2 shall apply only to generating installations using renewable energy sources with an installed electricity capacity of less than 200 kW.» Capacity mechanisms in place on the Regulation's date had a transition: «Member States that apply capacity mechanisms on 4 July 2019 shall adapt their mechanisms to comply with Chapter 4 without prejudice to commitments or contracts concluded by 31 December 2019.» Cross-border capacity: «At the request of the transmission system operators in a capacity calculation region, the relevant regulatory authorities may grant a derogation from paragraph 8 on foreseeable grounds».

*Analytical inference:* these exemptions concern generators and network operators. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any derogation applies to on-site generation at a business site.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5 June 2019: the Regulation was adopted
- 4 July 2019: capacity mechanisms apply the carbon limit to new capacity from this date at the latest
- 5 October 2019: transmission system operators to propose the bidding-zone review methodology (past)
- 31 December 2019: contracts concluded by this date are not affected by the capacity mechanism rules (past)
- 1 January 2020: the Regulation applies (in force)
- 5 January 2020: Member States report to the Commission on price-formation measures (past)
- 5 July 2020: ENTSO for Electricity submits methodologies to ACER (past)
- 1 January 2021: imbalance settlement period of 15 minutes in all scheduling areas (past)
- 5 July 2021: ENTSO for Electricity sets up the capacity registry (past)
- 1 July 2022: regional coordination centres enter into operation (past)
- 1 January 2025: imbalance settlement period no longer than 30 minutes where an exemption was granted (past)
- 1 July 2025: Commission review of network codes and guidelines, and capacity mechanism carbon limit for older capacity (past)
- 31 December 2025: minimum cross-zonal capacity reached (past)
- 1 January 2026: contract periods in the balancing market no longer than six months (in force)
- 31 December 2026: Commission legislative proposals, where appropriate
- 1 January 2028: regulators report on capacity covered by long contracts
- 31 December 2030: Commission review of the Regulation

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2023/2122 of 12 October 2023 amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 as regards updating the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions pursuant to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council», a European Union instrument that sets how emissions under the EU carbon-trading rules are measured and reported. Its subject matter after the change: «This Regulation shall apply to the monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions specified in relation to the activities listed in Annexes I and III to Directive 2003/87/EC, to activity data from stationary installations, to aviation activities and to released fuel amounts from activities referred to in Annex III to that Directive.» Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It was adopted on «Done at Brussels, 12 October 2023.» What the Regulation says is quoted from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*; points for counsel are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation rewrites the measuring-and-reporting rulebook for the EU emissions trading system. It follows a change to the Directive: «Following the amendment of Directive 2003/87/EC by Directives (EU) 2023/958» and Directive (EU) 2023/959. The parallel system itself comes from the amended Directive, and this Regulation adds the monitoring and reporting rules for it. The recitals say: «The amendment also introduces a separate but parallel emissions trading system applied to fuels used for combustion in the buildings and road transport sectors as well as in additional sectors which correspond to industrial activities not covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC». New monitoring rules sit in a new chapter for the companies that release fuel: «CHAPTER VIIa MONITORING OF EMISSIONS FROM REGULATED ENTITIES».

It takes effect as follows: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». «It shall apply from 1 January 2024.» «However, Article 1, points (24), (25)(a)(iii), (25)(d), (27), (30)(a), (31), (33), (34)(d) and (35) shall apply from 1 July 2024.» The rules count emissions from earlier: «It shall apply to emissions, activity data and released fuel amounts occurring from 1 January 2021.»

*Analytical inference:* road transport is named as a sector of the new emissions trading system, so a business that runs road vehicles is a consumer of fuel the new rules measure; the Regulation addresses the companies that release fuel and the operators of installations, aircraft and ships, and a forwarder is not named. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether and how any carbon cost under the new emissions trading system reaches the business through its fuel contracts.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: a second emissions trading system for fuels used in road transport and buildings is being set up, with reporting from 1 January 2025 and trading expected from 2027. The recitals give the timing: «In accordance with Directive (EU) 2023/959, surrendering of allowances under the new emissions trading system will only start in 2028 for the annual emissions of 2027.» «However, the monitoring and reporting of emissions under the new emissions trading system should start from 1 January 2025.» The recitals also say who may feel the cost: «To avoid unintended consequences regarding the levels of costs passed on to consumers, the use of default values lower than 1 should be subject to conditions, in particular after the start of trading in the new emissions trading system in 2027.» The recurring report date is: «From 2026, the regulated entity shall submit to the competent authority by 30 April of each year an emissions report that covers the annual emissions in the reporting period».

- A fuel-procurement lead asks each road-fuel supplier, before the start of trading in 2027, whether a carbon cost under the new emissions trading system will be shown on the invoice and how it is calculated, and records the answers by supplier.
- A pricing lead lists the road quotes whose delivery runs past the start of trading in 2027 and flags them for a fuel-cost clause.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the quoted recitals; the Regulation sets no price and states no rule for passing the cost to a customer, so the supplier answer is the only evidence. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a fuel-cost clause can lawfully pass a carbon cost to a client under the contracts the business holds.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

Two kinds of company carry the duties. For installations, aircraft and ships the term is operator; for fuel the term is regulated entity: «any reference to operator and aircraft operator shall be read as if it were a reference to the regulated entity». A regulated entity reports on who consumes the fuel: «Each regulated entity shall, together with their verified emission report in accordance with Article 75p(1), submit information on the consumers of the fuels it released for consumption as listed in Annex Xb.» Operators report in the other direction: «Each operator shall, together with their verified emission report in accordance with Article 68(1), submit information in accordance with Annex Xa.» The fuel streams the rules follow include «released for consumption through specific physical means, such as pipelines, trucks, rail, ships or fuel stations».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that buys road fuel is a consumer of released fuel and may be among the consumers a supplier reports on; the texts do not name a forwarder or a haulier as bound by these duties. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a regulated entity, an operator, or only a fuel consumer for each of its activities.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Annual report. «In 2025, the regulated entity shall submit to the competent authority by 30 April an emissions report that covers the annual emissions in 2024.» After that, «From 2026, the regulated entity shall submit to the competent authority by 30 April of each year an emissions report that covers the annual emissions in the reporting period and that is verified in accordance with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067.»

Categories. «a category A entity, where from 2027 to 2030 the average verified annual emissions in the 2 years preceding the reporting period, with the exclusion of CO 2 stemming from biomass, are equal to or less than 50 000 tonnes of CO 2(e)».

Improvement reports. «for any regulated entity that is using the default scope factor as referred to in Article 75l(3) and (4), by 31 July 2026».

Low emitters. «from 2027 to 2030 the average verified annual emissions in the 2 years preceding the reporting period, with the exclusion of CO 2 stemming from biomass, were less than 1 000 tonnes of CO 2 per year».

Default values. A regulated entity may apply a default value lower than 1 to determine the end use of fuel only on conditions, and from the start of 2027 a further condition is added: «for the purposes of reporting emissions in the reporting years as from 1 January 2027 the regulated entity demonstrates to the satisfaction of the competent authority that using default values lower than 1 leads to a more accurate determination of emissions and that at least one of the following conditions is met».

Exempt fuels. «the supply of solid wood fuels (CN-codes 4401 and 4402) and peat (CN code 2703) are currently not covered by the fuel definition of that Directive and are therefore also exempt from monitoring and reporting obligations under this Regulation».

Penalties. «Member States shall establish measures against fraud and determine the penalties to be imposed in the event of fraud which are commensurate with their purpose and which have an adequate deterrent effect.»

*Analytical inference:* these duties fall on regulated entities and operators; the text sets no duty on a business that only buys fuel, and the penalty is set by each Member State, not stated as an amount. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which category a regulated entity falls into, and whether any penalty reaches a fuel consumer.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reports run to the competent authority of the Member State. A regulated entity also has a planning step: «At the latest 4 months before a regulated entity commences the activity covered by Annex III to Directive 2003/87/EC, it shall submit to the competent authority a monitoring plan for approval». The first year of data is historical: «regulated entities are to report historical emissions for 2024». Operators of installations, and aircraft operators and shipping companies where relevant, report fuel details: «Reports on fuel suppliers and fuel use of stationary installations and, where relevant, aircraft operators and shipping companies».

*Analytical inference:* the registration and report duties fall on regulated entities and operators; none is stated on a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an aircraft operator or shipping company the business uses will pass any Annex Xa request to its customers.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the system work sits with fuel suppliers and operators, and the data link between them is mandatory. «Each regulated entity which releases fuel for combustion, in sectors covered by Chapter III of Directive 2003/87/EC, shall determine their emissions in the report referred to in Article 75p(1) of this Regulation by using the information from operator’s reports submitted in accordance with Annex Xa to this Regulation and by deducting the relevant amounts of fuels referred to in those reports.» The Member State side: «Member States shall facilitate the efficient exchanges of information which enable the regulated entities to determine the end use of the fuel released for consumption.»

- A fuel-procurement lead asks the road-fuel supplier, at the next contract review, which method it uses to determine the end use of the fuel it releases and whether it will ask the business for end-use data.

*Analytical inference:* the end-use information flows between operators, Member States and fuel suppliers; the text sets no duty on a business that only buys fuel, so the question to the supplier is how the supplier will meet its own duty. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a supplier may require end-use data from a customer under the contract.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Small emitters get lighter rules: «The competent authority may consider a regulated entity to be a regulated entity with low emissions where at least one of the following conditions is met». Fuel for sectors already in the older emissions trading system is handled to avoid double charging: «Where the released fuel amounts of a fuel stream are used only for combustion in sectors covered by Chapters II and III of Directive 2003/87/EC, with the exception of installations excluded under Article 27a of that Directive, the scope factor shall be set at zero».

*Analytical inference:* these are rules for how suppliers count fuel, and the text does not extend them to fuel consumers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any fuel the business buys falls under the exception.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «LEI Nº 14.993, DE 8 DE OUTUBRO DE 2024», a federal law of Brazil on low-carbon mobility fuels. The law describes itself: «Dispõe sobre a promoção da mobilidade sustentável de baixo carbono e a captura e a estocagem geológica de dióxido de carbono; institui o Programa Nacional de Combustível Sustentável de Aviação (ProBioQAV), o Programa Nacional de Diesel Verde (PNDV) e o Programa Nacional de Descarbonização do Produtor e Importador de Gás Natural e de Incentivo ao Biometano». Its main obligation reaches «Os operadores aéreos ficam obrigados a reduzir as emissões de GEE em suas operações domésticas por meio do uso de SAF». The source text is in Portuguese; quoted passages keep that wording and the surrounding lines are in English. The stored title of this item names the National Policy on Alternative Fuels (PNCA), a programme; the capture held is Lei 14.993/2024, and the name PNCA is not in it. What the Law says is quoted; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:*; points for counsel are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the text held ends partway through Article 11, so provisions after that point (including any article on entry into force and on penalties) are not part of this reading.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Law is a package of Brazilian fuel and emissions measures. Article 1 lists what it does: «Esta Lei: I - institui o Programa Nacional de Combustível Sustentável de Aviação (ProBioQAV), o Programa Nacional de Diesel Verde (PNDV) e o Programa Nacional de Descarbonização do Produtor e Importador de Gás Natural e de Incentivo ao Biometano;» It also «altera os limites máximo e mínimo do teor de mistura de etanol anidro à gasolina C comercializada ao consumidor final e do teor de mistura de biodiesel ao diesel comercializado ao consumidor final», and it joins existing programmes: «integra iniciativas e medidas adotadas no âmbito da Política Nacional de Biocombustíveis (RenovaBio), do Programa Mobilidade Verde e Inovação (Programa Mover), do Programa Brasileiro de Etiquetagem Veicular (PBEV) e do Programa de Controle de Emissões Veiculares (Proconve)».

For aviation, the aim of the sustainable aviation fuel programme is: «O ProBioQAV tem como objetivo incentivar a pesquisa, a produção, a comercialização e o uso energético, na matriz energética brasileira, do combustível sustentável de aviação».

The Law is dated «LEI Nº 14.993, DE 8 DE OUTUBRO DE 2024». The text held contains no article on when the Law enters into force, so the first dated obligation (section 3) is the earliest date it states.

*Analytical inference:* the Law's duties fall on air operators, the fuel agencies and ministries; a forwarder is not named in the text held, which is cut partway through Article 11. The text held does not give the new ethanol and biodiesel limits. *Legal Confirmation Required:* when the Law entered into force and whether its other chapters add duties for transport buyers.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the first mandatory cut in domestic airline emissions with sustainable aviation fuel starts on 1 January 2027, about two months from the date of this brief, so the questions below are best settled before it starts. «I – 1% (um por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2027» The text held states no cost figure and no charge to freight customers.

- A carrier-relations lead asks each airline that flies the business's domestic Brazil air freight, before 1 January 2027, whether a charge for the sustainable aviation fuel obligation will be added to air freight rates, how it is calculated, and from which flight date.
- A pricing lead adds a line for a possible sustainable aviation fuel charge to each domestic Brazil air quote for flights after 1 January 2027, and marks it as unconfirmed until the airline answers.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the quoted obligation and date; the Law states no pass-through to a customer, so the airline answer is the only evidence. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the airlines the business uses count as air operators under the Law, and whether a charge can be added to existing air freight contracts.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Law defines the party it binds: «operador aéreo: empresa constituída que explora ou se propõe a explorar aeronaves para prestação dos serviços de transporte aéreo regular e não regular». Supervision sits with the civil aviation agency: «Caberá à Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac), no exercício da competência prevista no inciso X do caput do art. 8º da Lei nº 11.182, de 27 de setembro de 2005: I - estabelecer a metodologia de cálculo de verificação da redução de emissões associadas ao uso de SAF e de outros meios alternativos a que se refere o § 2º deste artigo; e II - fiscalizar o cumprimento das obrigações previstas neste artigo pelos operadores aéreos.» The fuel agency sets the emission values: «A ANP estabelecerá os valores das emissões totais equivalentes por unidade de energia computados no ciclo do poço à queima de cada rota tecnológica de produção de SAF, para fins de contabilizar a descarbonização em face do querosene de aviação fóssil.»

*Analytical inference:* the Law does not name a forwarder as bound by the airline obligation; the text held states no cost figure and no effect on air freight rates, and it is cut partway through Article 11. The definition covers regular and non-regular air transport services and does not say whether cargo airlines are included. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether cargo operators are air operators under Article 2, item XVI.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The percentages can be changed: «O CNPE poderá alterar os percentuais de que trata o caput deste artigo, a qualquer tempo, por motivo justificado de interesse público, e, após a normalização das condições que motivaram a alteração, os referidos percentuais serão reestabelecidos». The Law also leaves rules to be written: «poderá ser estendida a voos de operadores aéreos internacionais com passagem pelo território nacional, com base no princípio da reciprocidade, mediante determinação do CNPE e posterior regulamentação da Anac». The life-cycle method for the linked fuel programmes changes: «I – ciclo do poço à roda até 31 de dezembro de 2031; e II – ciclo do berço ao túmulo a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2032».

*Analytical inference:* the CNPE power in paragraph 3 means the 2027 start and later percentages are not fixed; the Anac rules on verification are not in the text held. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the CNPE has altered any percentage or extended the obligation to international flights.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Airline obligation. «I – 1% (um por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2027; II – 2% (dois por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2029; III – 3% (três por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2030; IV – 4% (quatro por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2031; V – 5% (cinco por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2032; VI – 6% (seis por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2033; VII – 7% (sete por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2034; VIII – 8% (oito por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2035; IX – 9% (nove por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2036; X – 10% (dez por cento), a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2037».

Base of the calculation. «A base de cálculo sobre a qual serão computadas as obrigações de redução de emissões a que se refere o caput deste artigo será dada pelo volume das emissões decorrentes das operações domésticas realizadas pela empresa aérea no ano correspondente, supondo que todas as operações tenham utilizado combustível fóssil».

Other means. «Poderão ser admitidos meios alternativos para cumprimento da meta de que trata o caput deste artigo, nos termos do regulamento».

Fuel programmes. «Para fins de apuração do cumprimento das metas do Programa Mover, o Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE) fixará os valores de ICE e a participação dos combustíveis líquidos ou gasosos ou da energia elétrica».

Penalty. No penalty: the text held states no penalty, fine or sanction; Anac supervises compliance under Article 10, paragraph 5, and the text held ends partway through Article 11.

Scope and exceptions of the obligation. The scope is in the caput: «Os operadores aéreos ficam obrigados a reduzir as emissões de GEE em suas operações domésticas por meio do uso de SAF». The exceptions are in paragraphs 6 and 7: «A Anac poderá dispensar do cumprimento da obrigação prevista no caput deste artigo as operadoras aéreas: I - com emissões anuais inferiores à definida em regulação da Anac; II - sem acesso a SAF em nenhum dos aeroportos em que operem.» «O disposto neste artigo não gera prejuízo ou cumulatividade aos acordos setoriais ou regulamentos específicos que disponham sobre outras metas de redução de emissões de GEE.» The percentages can also change: «O CNPE poderá alterar os percentuais de que trata o caput deste artigo, a qualquer tempo, por motivo justificado de interesse público, e, após a normalização das condições que motivaram a alteração, os referidos percentuais serão reestabelecidos».

No exceptions are stated in Article 10, caput and paragraphs 1 and 2; the exceptions are in paragraphs 6 and 7. No scope limits are stated in Article 10, paragraphs 1 and 2; the domestic-operations scope is in the caput.

*Analytical inference:* the obligation falls on air operators on their domestic operations; the text held names no duty on a business that buys air freight, but it is cut partway through Article 11 and later articles are not read. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the airlines the business uses are air operators, and how the Law treats international flights, which Article 11 leaves to a later CNPE decision.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The text held names one registered certificate, for biomethane: «Certificado de Garantia de Origem de Biometano (CGOB): certificado de rastreabilidade lastreado em volume de biometano produzido e comercializado pelo produtor de biocombustível, emitido por agente certificador de origem credenciado pela ANP». For aviation, the verification method is left to Anac (section 4).

*Analytical inference:* the text held names no registration or reporting duty on a business that buys air freight or diesel, but it is cut partway through Article 11. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any registration duty in articles after Article 11 reaches a transport buyer.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: the obligation sits with airlines, and the first step is dated. A pricing system needs one new field before the first obligation date, 1 January 2027, because the cut is calculated per airline on domestic operations.

- A pricing lead adds a field for a sustainable aviation fuel charge to the domestic Brazil air quote template before quotes for flights after 1 January 2027 are issued, and fills it from the airline's written answer.

*Analytical inference:* the field rests on the Article 10 base of calculation, which counts the airline's own domestic emissions; the Law states no charge to customers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a charge may be shown as a separate line on a client quote.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Law lets Anac excuse some operators: «A Anac poderá dispensar do cumprimento da obrigação prevista no caput deste artigo as operadoras aéreas: I - com emissões anuais inferiores à definida em regulação da Anac; II - sem acesso a SAF em nenhum dos aeroportos em que operem.» The obligation does not stack with other targets: «O disposto neste artigo não gera prejuízo ou cumulatividade aos acordos setoriais ou regulamentos específicos que disponham sobre outras metas de redução de emissões de GEE.»

*Analytical inference:* the emissions level for the exemption is not in the text held, so which operators are excused cannot be read from it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an airline the business uses has been exempted by Anac.

- 1 January 2037: minimum cut reaches 10 %

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers «REGULATION (EU) 2023/435 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 February 2023 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/241 as regards REPowerEU chapters in recovery and resilience plans». It is a European Union regulation, so it reaches every Member State: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It changes the rules of a recovery funding facility and adds one article to the EU emissions trading directive. It is written for national governments and the Commission, not for freight businesses. What the text states is quoted between guillemets; what it means for a freight operator is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the text sets duties for Member States and the Commission and names no freight forwarder, carrier or shipper, so its effect on a freight business is indirect, through the funding it releases and the allowance auctions it orders.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation adds a new kind of chapter to national recovery plans. It is published in the Official Journal: «Official Journal of the European Union L 63/1». The funding it adds is described in these words: «shall be made available as additional non-repayable financial support under the Facility for implementation under this Regulation to increase the resilience of the Union’s energy system through a decrease of dependence on fossil fuels and diversifying energy supplies at Union level.» The money comes from selling emissions allowances: «As an extraordinary and one-time measure, until 31 August 2026, the allowances auctioned pursuant to paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article shall be auctioned until the total amount of revenue obtained from such auctioning has reached EUR 20 billion.»

What the money can pay for includes transport: «addressing internal and cross-border energy transmission and distribution bottlenecks, supporting electricity storage and accelerating the integration of renewable energy sources, and supporting zero-emission transport and its infrastructure, including railways». The Regulation enters into force as follows: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is affected only where it operates in or sells to a Member State whose recovery plan funds zero-emission transport and its infrastructure, including railways, or where it receives such funding itself. The text states no duty on a freight business.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: nothing in the text obliges a freight business to act within the next 30 days. The step that carries most value is to check where the funding lands. A funding lead, at the start of each quarter, lists each Member State in which the business runs rail terminals, road fleets or port-side energy use, and reads each national plan for a REPowerEU chapter that names zero-emission transport and its infrastructure.

The auction window has closed on the text's own date: «until 31 August 2026». The measure date for the security-of-supply exception is still ahead: «the measure is planned to be in operation by 31 December 2026».

*Analytical inference:* the first date has passed, so the allowance-funded part follows the schedule already set; the second is a date for Member States, not for a freight business. The business gains from a funded project only if the project is in a Member State where it trades.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names Member States, the Commission, the Council, the European Investment Bank and final recipients of funding. The auctioneer is named: «The EIB shall be the auctioneer for the allowances to be auctioned pursuant to this Article on the auction platform appointed pursuant to Article 26(1) of Regulation (EU) No 1031/2010 and shall provide the revenues generated from the auctioning to the Commission.» Each Member State must publish who receives the money: «Each Member State shall create an easy-to-use public portal containing data on the 100 final recipients receiving the highest amount of funding for the implementation of measures under the Facility.» A forwarder, carrier or shipper is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the chain unless it is a final recipient of Facility funding, for example as operator of a funded terminal or fleet project. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular grant or contract a client or the business holds is funding under the Facility, and so whether its recipient is published.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text schedules a review of the auction: «The period for auctioning referred to in this Article shall be reviewed one year after its start in the light of the impact of the auctioning provided for in this Article on the carbon market and price.» It also sets later quantities: «Until 31 August 2026, a number of allowances from the quantity which would otherwise be auctioned from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2030 by the Member States under Article 10(2), point (a), shall be auctioned to support the objectives set out in Article 21c(3), points (b) to (f), of Regulation (EU) 2021/241 until the amount of revenue obtained from such auctioning has reached EUR 8 billion.»

*Analytical inference:* the review is the point where the effect of these auctions on the carbon market and price is examined; the text states no result of that review and no price effect.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Chapter duty. «Recovery and resilience plans submitted to the Commission after 1 March 2023 that require the use of additional funding under Articles 14, 21a or 21b, shall include a REPowerEU chapter containing measures and their corresponding milestones and targets.»

Qualifying measures. «The measures in the REPowerEU chapter shall be either new reforms and investments, started from 1 February 2022 onwards, or the scaled-up part of reforms and investments included in the already adopted Council implementing decision for the Member State concerned.»

Loan communication. «Member States shall communicate to the Commission by 31 March 2023, whether they intend to request loan support.»

Environmental condition. «the principle of “do no significant harm” shall not apply to the reforms and investments under paragraph 3, point (a), of this Article, subject to a positive assessment by the Commission».

Fund support. «It should be possible that those Funds provide support to the REPowerEU objectives where such support falls within the scope of the Fund concerned».

Pre-financing. «the Commission shall make the pre-financing payments, to the extent possible and subject to available resources».

Transparency. «Member States shall update those data twice a year.»

Penalty. The Regulation sets no penalty, fine or sanction for a Member State or a business that does not meet these duties.

*Analytical inference:* every duty above falls on a Member State or the Commission, the party each span names; none falls on a freight business. No phase-in is stated in Articles 21a to 21d and 25a.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national rule that implements a REPowerEU chapter places a duty or a condition on a freight business that receives funding.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 1; extracted as FACT: 7.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

A Member State must publish funding recipients: «in the case of a legal person, the recipient’s full legal name and VAT identification number or tax identification number, where available, or another unique identifier established at the national level», and «the amount received by each recipient, as well as the associated measures for which a Member State has received funding under the Facility». Personal data come down later: «Where personal data are published, the information referred to in paragraph 2 shall be removed by the Member State concerned two years after the end of the financial year in which the funding has been paid to the final recipient.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that becomes one of the highest-funded recipients in a Member State would appear by name with its tax identifier and the amount received. The text asks the business for no filing.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text requires no system build by a freight business. A grants lead keeps, when a funded project is announced and for any project funded under a national recovery plan, a record of the legal entity that received the money, its VAT or tax identifier and the amount, because the Member State publishes those items for the highest-funded recipients. The published item is «the recipient’s full legal name and VAT identification number or tax identification number, where available».

*Analytical inference:* the record lets the business check its own entry and answer a client who asks why a project partner appears on a public portal. The text states no right to correct the entry.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 27 February 2023: Regulation adopted at Brussels, «Done at Brussels, 27 February 2023.»
- 1 March 2023: enters into force the day after publication in the Official Journal; commitment appropriations are made available «as of 1 March 2023»
- 31 March 2023: Member States communicate whether they intend to request loan support, date passed
- 31 August 2023: loan support requests may still be made, «request loan support until 31 August 2023», date passed
- 31 December 2023: Council implementing decision needed for pre-financing, «by 31 December 2023», date passed
- 31 August 2026: end of the one-time auction window, «until 31 August 2026», date passed
- 31 December 2026: security-of-supply measures are planned to be in operation, «planned to be in operation by 31 December 2026»
- 31 December 2030: end of the period in which 27 million unallocated market stability reserve allowances are used to support innovation, «until 31 December 2030, 27 million unallocated allowances»
- 2050: EU climate neutrality objective, «objective of EU climate neutrality by 2050»

   "body": "## 1. What's Moving and What Triggered It

MONITORING: this item follows the supply of the minerals in electric vehicle batteries, and the trade rules around them. Signal event: «Critical minerals, which are essential for a range of energy technologies and for the broader economy, have become a major focus in global policy and trade discussions.» The International Energy Agency explains why it tracks them: «Price volatility, supply chain bottlenecks and geopolitical concerns make the regular monitoring of their supply and demand extremely vital.» A peer-reviewed analysis of United States tailpipe standards states the need: «First, the proposed standard necessitates replacing at least 10.21 million new internal combustion engine vehicles with EVs between 2027 and 2032.» It then finds a gap between the minerals available and that need: «Third, mineral production capacities in the United States and amongst allies support the deployment of 5.09 million vehicles between 2027 and 2032, well short of compliance target.» The trade side comes from a World Trade Organization blog by UN Trade and Development staff: «In general, the tariffs on battery packs and EVs are considerably higher than those on raw minerals and battery minerals, with a clear pattern of tariff escalation moving up the value chain.»

*Analytical inference:* the four passages describe constraints and tariffs, not a price move; none of the pages read gives a mineral price, a price change or a date on which one happens, so this brief states no price trend. The pages hold no competitor or technology launch, so the brief serves the cost, trade-rule, client and regulatory-link lenses only.

## 2. Who's Driving It and What They Want

Driving parties: the United States rules come from an agency named in the analysis: «introduced by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 2023» The analysis also says that influence over supply is held by some states: «some countries levy disproportional influence over key aspects of the automotive supply chain». The trade blog names the economies with the minerals: «Developing economies with rich mineral resources stand to benefit from the increase in demand for cobalt, graphite and lithium, but a well-functioning multilateral trading system, supported by a fair system of tariffs at a lower level, is essential to enable these economies to participate more fully in the global EV value chain.» The International Energy Agency publishes the supply and demand outlook: «provides a snapshot of recent industry developments from 2024 and early 2025 and offers medium- and long-term projections for the supply and demand of key energy minerals».

*Analytical inference:* the pages state the wants of mineral-producing economies (a lower and flatter tariff system) and of the United States standard (more electric vehicle sales); they name no carrier, shipper or forwarder and state no interest of a market party in freight.

## 3. Expected Trajectory and Conversion Triggers

Conversion trigger: a dated United States rule ties tax credit eligibility to where battery minerals come from: «The US Inflation Reduction Act sets that in 2027, for an electric vehicle to be tax-credit eligible, 80% of the market value of critical minerals in its battery must be sourced domestically, from US free-trade partners or from North American recycling.» The same page says the target's viability is evaluated, not settled: «The viability of the target is evaluated for different battery chemistries.»

- 2027: «in 2027, for an electric vehicle to be tax-credit eligible, 80% of the market value of critical minerals in its battery must be sourced domestically»
- 2032: «82 grams/mile (g/mile) of CO 2 by 2032»

*Analytical inference:* the 2032 target is for the light-duty fleet and the 2027 rule is for the tax-credit eligibility of an electric vehicle, in the United States, as the quoted sentences say; neither page states that they apply to electric trucks or to goods moved by freight. The pages held do not state whether the 2027 United States credit rule still applies. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the credit rule or the tailpipe standard applies to any vehicle or battery a client imports into the United States.

## 4. Operational and Cost Implications If It Materializes

The cause the pages state is mineral scarcity and tariff escalation. On scarcity: «Fifth, limited production of battery-grade graphite and cobalt may represent particularly profound constraints.» On demand: «Projections suggest a fivefold increase in demand for these minerals by 2050 due to their intensive use in new energy technologies.» On the value chain, the blog lists where the goods are classified: «4. Manufacturing of battery cells and packs. 850760 850790 5. Production of electric and hybrid vehicles. 870240 870360 870370 870380». And on tariffs: «More than three-quarters of the economies surveyed exhibit rising tariffs from the first to the fifth processing stages although the extent varies widely.» Corridor identity: the pages name no origin-destination port pair and no transport mode together, so no lane is tied to this signal.

*Analytical inference:* the blog places battery cells and packs and electric vehicles in the highest-tariff stages, so in general a consignment of battery packs or vehicles meets a higher applied duty than one of raw minerals, though the blog says the extent varies widely between economies; a customs broker's classification of the consignment by the codes above is the first step to the rate that applies, and the blog gives no rate for any consignment. The pages state no freight rate, surcharge or transit time effect, so the effect by cargo vertical needs data that the pages do not hold.

## 5. Competitive Implications

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the pages name no competitor and no operator position.*

## 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

- Say that the cost of battery minerals and the tariff on battery packs and electric vehicles are two separate pressures: «In general, the tariffs on battery packs and EVs are considerably higher than those on raw minerals and battery minerals», and the blog says «although the extent varies widely».
- Ask a client that ships battery packs or electric vehicles which classification code it declares, using the codes the blog lists.
- Do not present the United States credit threshold as a settled requirement for any client: «The viability of the target is evaluated for different battery chemistries.»
- Do not state a mineral price move to a client; no price is held.

## 7. What the Workspace Should Do Now

Action now: MONITORING: a customs lead, at the next quarterly review of the tariff table, records for each battery cell, battery pack and electric vehicle code a client declares the applied duty rate by origin and the value chain stage, so that a change in the tariff step between stages shows up as a change in duty on a named consignment.

- A contract lead adds, at the next renewal with a client that ships battery packs or electric vehicles, a clause that names who pays a change in applied duty between order and arrival.
- A data lead keeps, from now, one record per consignment of battery cells, battery packs or electric vehicles with its classification code, origin and declared value, so a later tariff or credit change can be priced from history.

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the stage-by-stage tariff pattern and the code list quoted in section 4; they position the business and do not respond to a dated duty.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COUNCIL IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2026/1295 of 4 June 2026 authorising Sweden to apply reduced rates of excise duty to gas oil and unleaded petrol used as motor fuels, in accordance with Article 19 of Directive 2003/96/EC». Where this framework applies: Sweden only, because «This Decision is addressed to the Kingdom of Sweden.» The Decision lets Sweden charge less excise duty, a tax set per litre of fuel, on diesel and petrol for five months. What the Decision says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

EU rules set a floor under the excise duty each Member State charges on fuel, and Article 19 of Directive 2003/96/EC lets the Council authorise one Member State to go below it. This Decision gives Sweden that authorisation: «Sweden is authorised to apply a reduction of the rates up to 2,4 SEK per litre below the minimum levels of taxation referred to in Article 7 of Directive 2003/96/EC for gas oil and unleaded petrol used as motor fuels.» The reason the Council gives: «In the weeks preceding the adoption of this Decision, sharp and persistent increases in wholesale and retail prices of energy products were observed across the Union, triggered by geopolitical developments in the Middle East, which have affected supply chains of oil and oil products globally.» Sweden asked for it: «By letter dated 26 March 2026, in accordance with Article 19 of Directive 2003/96/EC, the Swedish authorities requested authorisation to apply reduced rates of excise duty to gas oil and unleaded petrol used as motor fuels.» The Council records the length asked for: «The authorisation was requested for a period of five months.» The Council says what such a cut does: «Temporary reductions in the taxation of targeted energy products can provide rapid relief to households and undertakings by directly lowering end-user prices.»

When this framework enters into force: «This Decision shall take effect on the date of its notification.» The period in which it applies is stated as «This Decision shall apply from 1 July 2026 until 30 November 2026.»

The Council also gives general reasoning on untargeted tax reductions, which is not a statement about the size or cost of this Decision's measure: «untargeted tax reductions imply significant fiscal costs and tend to increase fossil fuel demand, thereby exacerbating the imbalance of supply and demand. Therefore, the measure should remain strictly limited in time.»

*Analytical inference:* the Decision says Sweden may cut the rate by up to 2,4 SEK per litre, so it sets a ceiling on the cut and not the Swedish rate itself. It does not state whether Sweden applies the cut, what the Swedish rate is, or whether a fuel seller or carrier passes a lower duty on to a buyer, so the effect on a freight quote is not stated. Road legs that take on diesel or petrol in Sweden are the freight activity closest to it.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the authorisation has applied since 1 July 2026 and has a fixed end: «This Decision shall apply from 1 July 2026 until 30 November 2026.» Any Swedish fuel cost built on the lower duty has a date after which the Decision no longer covers it.

- A pricing lead, at the next quote run, marks every quote for a road leg fuelled in Sweden whose fuel cost assumes the lower duty, and writes 30 November 2026 on it as the date to re-check that fuel cost.
- A carrier-relations lead asks each carrier on Swedish road legs, before 30 November 2026, whether its fuel charge now reflects the lower duty and what charge it will apply once the Decision stops applying.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the end date in Article 2; the Decision itself asks nothing of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a contract that ties a fuel charge to the Swedish pump price lets the carrier change the charge when the authorisation ends.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision names the Council, the Commission, the Swedish authorities and Sweden. It is addressed to one State: «This Decision is addressed to the Kingdom of Sweden.» The businesses it mentions are named only as those hit by the price rise: «on undertakings, including small and medium-sized enterprises». It names no carrier, forwarder or shipper, and it assigns no role in a supply chain.

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder is not named, so it meets the Decision only as a buyer of fuel or through a carrier that buys fuel in Sweden. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party in a Swedish road move bears the fuel excise duty, and whether a lower rate reaches the forwarder's cost under its contracts.
