   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers the way the European Union's emissions trading system applies to aviation, taken from the Commission's own aviation page. «Under the EU ETS, all airlines operating in Europe, European and non-European alike, are required to monitor, report and verify their emissions, and to surrender allowances against those emissions.» The reach of the scheme is set by geography: «The EU, however, decided to temporarily limit the scope of the EU ETS to flights within the EEA, to support the development of a global measure by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).»

The duties described run to airlines, which the page also calls aircraft operators. A freight forwarder is not named on the page. What the page states is set out as fact; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each question for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. A date the page gives that has since passed is written here as past.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The scheme is a cap-and-trade system for carbon dioxide, and aviation has been inside it for years: «since 2012, the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) has been covering the aviation sector in Europe». The mechanism is that «They receive tradeable allowances covering a certain level of emissions from their flights each year.» Compliance is high: «The compliance rate in the aviation sector is high, as over 99.5% of emissions are usually covered by surrender of allowances.»

The aviation rules were revised in 2023. The legal texts the page lists are «Directive (EU) 2023/958» and the «Consolidated version of the ETS Directive (EU) 2003/87/EC». The effective date of the 2023 revision, the day it enters into force, is stated by the page: «These rules were adopted on 10 May 2023 and entered into force on 5 June 2023.» The page gives the aim of the revision: «The revision of the EU ETS in aviation aims to ensure that the aviation industry contributes to the EU's climate objectives.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties above fall on airlines operating flights inside the scheme's geography. A forwarder meets the scheme where a booked flight is flown by an airline that holds those duties; the page states no charge passed from an airline to a customer, so the effect on an air freight rate is a gap in what the page holds.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: the page states the end of free allowances for airlines and that step is now reached: «Free allocation to aircraft operators will be reduced by 25% in 2024 and by 50% 2025, moving to full auctioning for the sector by 2026.» From 2026 an airline buys its allowances at auction instead of receiving some free. The page does not say whether airlines add this cost to air freight rates, so the cost reaching a forwarder's invoice is not stated.

- A carrier-relations lead asks each airline on the business's air rate agreements, at the next rate review, whether the move to full auctioning is added to the air freight rate and how any such charge is calculated.
- A pricing lead marks each air quote on a leg between two airports in the European Economic Area as inside the scheme, and records the airline's answer beside it.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the page's statement that airlines surrender allowances and that free allocation ends; the page requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any scheme cost may be charged on to a client under the business's own contracts.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The page names several parties. Airlines, called aircraft operators, hold the monitoring, reporting and allowance duties. Each is administered by a state: «Moreover, under the 'one-stop shop' approach, aircraft operators are administered by either an EEA state or Switzerland for both emission trading systems.» The Commission runs the system for other climate effects, and «EUROCONTROL will act as System Administrator of NEATS, undertaking the responsibility of hosting it.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder is not named in this role list, so the page places it outside the direct chain; it meets the scheme through the airline that flies its cargo. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party is the aircraft operator for a flight a client books, and whether any duty reaches a forwarder that sells air freight under its own name.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The page carries the Commission's answers on the reporting of climate effects other than carbon dioxide. One answer fixes the start of the duty: «The aircraft operator is required to undertake the Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) procedure as of 1 January 2025.» Another covers the tool delay: «NEATS will perform the CO 2 (e) calculation per flight retroactively for the period of its unavailability.»

*Analytical inference:* the answers set out how airlines report; they state no step for a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client or airline may ask a forwarder for flight data to support this reporting.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission set a review of flights to and from Europe: «By July 2026, the Commission will carry out an assessment of whether more action is required for flights to and from Europe, in line with criteria set in the EU ETS Directive». That date has passed and the page holds no outcome of the assessment. What could follow: «Subject to the outcome of this assessment, the Commission will make a legislative proposal that could extend the scope of EU emissions trading to departing flights and exempt incoming flights.»

The page also reports a newer proposal: «On 17 July 2026, the European Commission proposed a targeted revision of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)», which «strengthens the existing ETS for aviation and maritime transport». The page states that it will be updated with detail, and the detail is not held.

Two further steps are set. The geographic limit lapses: «The 2023 revision of the EU ETS aviation rules extended the restriction of the EU ETS geographical scope until the start of 2027.» And the Commission reports on the other climate effects: «By the end of 2027, the Commission will deliver a report on the results and if appropriate, will make a legislative proposal to address non-CO 2 effects of aviation.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2027 steps are the points where the rules for flights to and from non-EEA airports may change; the page gives no content for the outcome. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the proposal of July 2026 changes any duty a client or airline expects to rely on.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the page sets no threshold question in dispute for aviation beyond the scope limits shown in Section 12.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Allowances and reporting. «Under the EU ETS, all airlines operating in Europe, European and non-European alike, are required to monitor, report and verify their emissions, and to surrender allowances against those emissions.»

Allowance cost path. «Full auctioning from 2026 Free allocation to aircraft operators will be reduced by 25% in 2024 and by 50% 2025, moving to full auctioning for the sector by 2026.»

Penalty. «Article 16 of the EU ETS Directive establishes a limited harmonisation of the financial penalties that will be paid by operators that fail to surrender the necessary number of emissions allowances (i.e. €100 per tonne of CO 2 ).» Beyond that figure the Member States set the rest: «the co-legislators decided that the Member States should adopt rules on penalties for breaches of national legislation which transpose the Directive's requirements».

International flights. «The Directive maintains the current EU ETS scope and applies CORSIA to extra-European flights only, as stronger action is being taken for intra-European flights.»

Other climate effects. «Airline operators would start monitoring the non-CO 2 aviation effects from 1 January 2025, and reporting once a year.»

Exemption for outermost regions. «The current exemption in Article 3c(8) EU ETS Directive exempts domestic flights to and from OMR from the obligation of surrender (Article 12(3)), CO 2 reporting (Article 14(3)) and penalties (Article 16) until 31 December 2030, but not from non-CO 2 reporting (Article 14(5)).»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above is stated for the airline; the page states no pass-through of allowance cost to a customer, so the effect on a forwarder's costs rests on airline terms the page does not hold.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these airline duties, or the penalty for not surrendering allowances, creates a charge or liability for a forwarder or its client.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 1; extracted as FACT: 7.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the scheme sets airline duties, not duties on products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Emissions are reported once a year and checked: «The operator submits the verified emissions report to the administering Member State by 31 March of year X+1.» The same passage adds that «The operator must surrender sufficient emissions allowances to cover its emissions in calendar year X.» For the other climate effects the report content is set: «The annual emissions report will provide the sum of CO 2 (e) of the monitored flights of the aircraft operator per aerodrome pair.» The monitoring plan has its own timing: «The relevant timelines for submission of the Monitoring Plan to Competent Authorities are those in the Article 52(1) of the MRR.»

*Analytical inference:* these registration and report duties sit with the airline and its administering state; the page states none on a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder must supply shipment or flight data to an airline for these reports.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the system work sits with airlines and the Commission, and the page names no system a forwarder must build. The page sets the widening of reporting of climate effects other than carbon dioxide: «After this period, from January 2027, the monitoring and reporting requirement will be mandatory for all inbound and outbound flights to the EEA.» The calculation tool is hosted centrally: «NEATS is not envisaged to be installed on the aircraft operator cloud.»

- A compliance lead adds the January 2027 widening of reporting to the next review of the business's air carrier agreements, and asks each airline on those agreements whether it will request flight or shipment data from customers.

*Analytical inference:* the widening to all inbound and outbound flights is the point at which flights from and to non-EEA airports join the reporting, and the page states no data request to customers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract allows an airline or client to require data from the forwarder for this reporting.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Several flights and operators are treated differently. Arrivals from two neighbours: «Flights arriving from the UK were exempted in a Commission Delegated Regulation , similarly to flights arriving from Switzerland, as they are covered by the UK-ETS.» Small operators: «Aircraft operators emitting less than 25 000 tonnes of CO 2 per year, both commercial and non-commercial, can choose an alternative to verification by an independent verifier.» Outermost regions are set out in Section 8.

*Analytical inference:* a flight arriving from the United Kingdom or from Switzerland is outside the scheme's coverage of arrivals while a departure to the United Kingdom is covered, as the page states. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular route a client uses falls under one of these exemptions.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The page holds support and research measures beside the scheme. Fuel support: «20 million ETS allowances (EUR 1.6 bn at an allowance price of EUR 80) have been reserved to cover some, or all, of the price gap between conventional fossil fuels and eligible alternative aviation fuels uplifted from January 2024.» Innovation Fund: «The Innovation Fund can explicitly support the electrification of aviation, decarbonise the sector and mitigate its non-CO 2 effects.» Research funding: «a recent Horizon Europe call , open from December 2023 to April 2024, focused on projects aiming to minimising the non-CO 2 effects of aviation». The international scheme CORSIA is the alternative regime for flights outside the EEA, as Section 8 shows.

*Analytical inference:* these are funding and research measures for airlines and the sector; the page states no effect on air freight rates. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any client or airline claims support under these measures.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2012: the EU Emissions Trading System starts covering the aviation sector in Europe (in force)
- 5 June 2023: the revised aviation rules entered into force
- 2024: free allocation to aircraft operators reduced by 25% (past)
- 1 January 2025: monitoring of climate effects other than carbon dioxide starts for airlines (past)
- 2025: free allocation to aircraft operators reduced by 50% (past)
- 1 January 2026: full auctioning for aviation, no free allocation (the page gives the year, 2026; in force)
- July 2026: Commission assessment of flights to and from Europe due (date passed, outcome not held)
- 17 July 2026: Commission proposal for a targeted revision of the system (proposal, not law)
- 1 January 2027: monitoring and reporting of climate effects other than carbon dioxide mandatory for all inbound and outbound flights to the EEA (the page gives the month, January 2027)
- 2027: Commission report on the other climate effects of aviation due by the end of the year
- 31 December 2030: end of the exemption for domestic flights to and from outermost regions

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers the European Union rules on moving waste across borders: «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1157 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 April 2024 on shipments of waste, amending Regulations (EU) No 1257/2013 and (EU) 2020/1056 and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006». Its reach is stated in four lines: «This Regulation applies to: (a) shipments of waste between Member States, with or without transit through third countries; (b) shipments of waste imported into the Union from third countries; (c) shipments of waste exported from the Union to third countries; (d) shipments of waste in transit through the Union on the way to or from third countries.»

What the text states is set out as fact. What it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each question for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. Commission web pages are used for dates the Regulation leaves to practice, and an industry body's view is labelled as that. A date that has passed is written as past.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The aim is environmental: «This Regulation lays down measures to protect the environment and human health and to contribute to climate neutrality and to achieving a circular economy and zero pollution by preventing or reducing the adverse impacts which can result from shipments of waste and from the treatment of the waste at its destination.» The method is a set of routes by type of waste: «It establishes procedures and control regimes for shipments of waste, depending on the origin, destination and route of the shipment, the type of waste and the type of treatment to be applied to the waste at its destination.»

It replaces the earlier rules: «Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 is repealed with effect from 20 May 2024.» The old rules still run for a time: «However, the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 shall continue to apply until 21 May 2026 except for: (a) Article 30 that shall cease to apply from 20 May 2024; (b) Article 37 that shall continue to apply until 21 May 2027; (c) Article 51 that shall continue to apply until 31 December 2025.»

The effective date is split. «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». The Commission gives the date: «The new Regulation on waste shipments entered into force on 20 May 2024». Application follows: «It shall apply from 21 May 2026.» The Commission summarises the split: «most provisions apply from 21 May 2026 and most export rules will apply from 21 May 2027».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business meets the Regulation wherever it books, moves, clears or documents a load that is waste, since the scope covers shipments between Member States, imports, exports and transit. Whether a given load is waste is a threshold question, set out in Section 7.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

ACTION REQUIRED: the text sets a prohibition that applies from «(c) Article 39 point (1)(d) from 21 November 2026». Article 39 covers «Exports from the Union of the following wastes destined for recovery in countries to which the OECD Decision does not apply shall be prohibited» and point (d) is «plastic waste classified under entry B3011». The Commission confirms it for a wider group: «exports of plastic waste from the EU to non-OECD countries will be banned».

- A waste-freight desk lead reviews every open booking of plastic waste under entry B3011 that is bound for a country outside the OECD Decision, and stops those with a planned export from 21 November 2026.
- A shipment-operations lead confirms with each client that sends waste under the prior consent procedure that the notification and movement documents run through the electronic system, because the Commission states «While PIC procedures may now only be executed electronically», with a longer period for one group: «operators may continue to use the old paper procedure until 31 December 2026».
- A transport-operations lead checks that each carrier booked for a waste load can hold the documents in the vehicle when they cannot be shown online, as Section 8 sets out.

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the Article 39 prohibition, the Commission's statement on electronic procedures and the carrier duty in Articles 16 and 18; the text states no cost of a stopped booking. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is the person who arranges the shipment, a carrier or neither for each load.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the roles it needs. The notifier is the party that carries out or has a notified shipment carried out, and the person who arranges the shipment is «any of the following natural or legal persons under the national jurisdiction of the country of dispatch, who carries out or plans to carry out a shipment as referred to in Article 4(4) or (5), or who has or plans to have such a shipment carried out». The consignee is «any natural or legal person under the national jurisdiction of the country of destination to whom or to which the waste is shipped for recovery or disposal». The carrier is named in the duties of Sections 8 and 11, and authorities may reach it: «the authorities involved in inspections may require the notifier, the person who arranges the shipment, the waste holder, the carrier, the consignee and the facility that receives the waste to submit relevant documentary evidence to them within a period specified by them, and may detain the waste in a shipment and, when necessary, the means of transport containing the waste, as well as suspend the transport of the waste until such documentation has been provided». Authorities may also ask about the carriage itself: «may require the natural or legal person who is in possession of the substance or object concerned, or who arranges the carriage thereof, to submit documentary evidence».

If a shipment is illegal the costs follow a set order: «Costs arising from the take-back or recovery or disposal in an alternative way of waste from an illegal shipment, including costs for its transport of waste, recovery or disposal, pursuant to Article 25(2) or (3) and, from date on which the competent authority of dispatch becomes aware that a shipment is illegal, storage costs pursuant to Article 25(12), shall be charged to» the notifier or the person deemed to be the notifier first.

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder is not named as a role; it falls in the chain as a carrier, as the person who arranges the carriage, or through the client that is the notifier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role the business holds for each type of load, because the carrier duties and the evidence requests above attach to named roles.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Commission's own pages explain the electronic system and the transition. On the launch: «The revised Waste Shipment Regulation and most of its provisions enter into application today (21 May), including the launch of the Digital Waste Shipment System (DIWASS).» The Commission also lists «Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/2571 establishing the information to be provided in the certificate confirming the completion of a subsequent interim or non-interim recovery operation or a subsequent interim or non-interim disposal». It names the interoperability rules: «Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1290 on interoperability requirements for the digital waste shipment system». On plastics it says «From today, all plastic waste exports to third countries will require PIC approval.» On electronic waste, the classification comes from delegated acts that amend the Regulation, not from the Regulation itself; the Commission says «This new classification is effective from 1 January 2025.» and «The export of all e-waste from the EU to non-OECD countries is prohibited».

*Analytical inference:* the Commission pages describe how the Regulation is put into practice and do not replace its text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular load falls under the electronic waste entries or the plastic waste entry.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Several Commission steps are set by date. The list of countries that may receive non-hazardous waste: «The list referred to in paragraph 1 shall be adopted by 21 November 2026, unless no country submits a request pursuant to Article 42(1) or no country complies with the requirements set out in Article 42(3) at that time.» The Commission's page adds «A first list of authorised countries will be established by 21 November 2026, and exports to non-OECD countries not on the list will be prohibited.» and says the first list is planned for November 2026, so no list is held in the item's material.

Other dates: «By 21 May 2027, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act establishing detailed criteria for the uniform application of the conditions laid down in paragraph 1, point (a)»; «By 21 May 2028, the Commission shall incorporate a function into the central system referred to in Article 27(3), which provides courtesy translations of the communications referred to in paragraph 1.»; «The report mentioned in the first subparagraph shall be drawn up for the first time by 31 December 2029 and every three years thereafter.»; and «By 31 December 2035, the Commission shall, taking into account, inter alia, the reports drawn up in accordance with Article 73, and the review referred to in Article 62(5), carry out a review of this Regulation». Two earlier steps are past: «By 21 August 2024, the Commission shall contact all countries to which the OECD Decision does not apply» and «At the latest by 21 May 2025, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts to establish:». Two further steps are past: «The Commission shall by 21 May 2026 assess whether countries to which the OECD Decision applies and which import significant volumes of plastic waste from the Union comply with this Article.» and «By 21 May 2026, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 80 to supplement this Regulation by setting out instructions on how to complete the Annex VII document.» The item's material holds no outcome of either.

*Analytical inference:* the list of countries, the 2027 criteria and the Annex VII instructions decide which exports can continue and how forms are filled in, so the practical rules are not settled by the text alone. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the delegated act and the list have been published since the capture.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question is whether a load is waste at all. Authorities may require proof: «In order to ascertain that a substance or object being carried by road, rail, air, sea or inland waterway is not waste, the authorities involved in inspections may require the natural or legal person who is in possession of the substance or object concerned, or who arranges the carriage thereof, to submit documentary evidence». If the proof is missing the effect is stated: «Where the authorities have concluded that a substance or object is waste in accordance with the first subparagraph, the carriage of the substance or object concerned or the shipment of waste concerned shall be considered as an illegal shipment.»

The second question is which route applies. Disposal is barred unless consent is obtained: «Shipments of all wastes destined for disposal shall be prohibited, except if consent is obtained in accordance with Article 11.» The lighter route has a size trigger: «Shipments of the following wastes destined for recovery shall be subject to the general information requirements laid down in Article 18, if the quantity of waste shipped exceeds 20 kg».

*Analytical inference:* the waste test and the route test decide which documents a load needs before it moves. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular used-goods or scrap load is waste under the Regulation and which route it takes.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Routes. «Shipments of all wastes destined for disposal shall be prohibited, except if consent is obtained in accordance with Article 11.»

Documents on the road. «Where the documents referred to in paragraphs 1 and 3 cannot be made available online during the transport of waste, the notifier and the carrier or carriers shall ensure that the documents are available by other means in the transport vehicle.» The lighter route has the same duty: «Where the information referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 cannot be made available online during the transport of waste, the person who arranges the shipment and the carrier or carriers shall ensure that the information is available by other means in the transport vehicle». Timing: «The person who arranges the shipment shall complete the form set out in Annex VII with the relevant information to the extent possible, no later than two working days before the shipment starts.»

Electronic exchange. «The following information and documents shall be submitted and exchanged by electronic means, via the hub of the central system referred to in paragraph 3 or via other available interoperable systems or software in accordance with paragraph 4».

Export limits. «Exports from the Union of the following wastes destined for recovery in countries to which the OECD Decision does not apply shall be prohibited», including «plastic waste classified under entry B3011». For non-hazardous waste the limit is lifted only for listed countries: «Paragraph 1 shall not apply to exports of wastes or mixtures of wastes destined for recovery to a country included in the list of countries established in accordance with Article 41, for the non-hazardous wastes and mixtures of non-hazardous wastes specified in that list.» From 21 May 2027 the exporter must show sound management: «The notifier or the person who arranges the shipment shall only export waste from the Union if it can demonstrate that the facilities which are to receive the waste in the country of destination will manage it in an environmentally sound manner as referred to in Article 59.» and «carried out no longer than two years prior to exporting waste to the facility concerned» for the audit.

Further limits and dates: «(f) wastes or mixtures of wastes containing or contaminated with POPs in quantities meeting or exceeding a concentration limit indicated in Annex IV to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021» is also barred, and the application dates are «(d) Articles 38(2) point (b), Article 40, Article 44(2) point (a), and Articles 46 and 47 from 21 May 2027, except for Article 40(3)(b) which shall apply from 21 May 2026».

Penalties. «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are applied. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» The minimum range is «The Member States shall at least be able to impose the following penalties in case of infringements of this Regulation, where relevant: (a) fines; (b) revocation or time-limited suspension of the authorisation to carry out activities related to management and shipment of waste insofar as these activities fall under the scope of this Regulation; (c) time-limited exclusion from public procurement procedures.»

*Analytical inference:* the carrier duty, the export prohibition and the inspection power act on named roles; the text states no storage, delay or demurrage cost for a held load and no pass-through to a client, so those are gaps. No phase-in is stated in Articles 16 and 18 beyond the dates quoted in Section 14.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these duties, or a penalty, reaches the business as a carrier or as the person who arranges the carriage.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation governs waste shipments by any holder and sets no list of products a freight business sells under its own name.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The person who arranges a lighter-route shipment needs a permit or registration: «A shipment referred to in paragraph 1 may only be arranged by the person who arranges the shipment referred to in Article 3, points (7)(ii), (iii) and (iv), when that person has obtained a permit or is registered in accordance with Chapter IV of Directive 2008/98/EC.» Member States report: «The report mentioned in the first subparagraph shall be drawn up for the first time by 31 December 2029 and every three years thereafter.» The reporting article applies earlier: «(e) Article 73 from 1 January 2026».

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties sit with the arranging party and with Member States; the text states none on a carrier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client expects the business to hold a registration or to supply data for the client's own shipment records.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: the electronic route is now in place and the paper route for one group ends. «operators may continue to use the old paper procedure until 31 December 2026» is the Commission's statement for green-listed waste, which it describes as «non-hazardous waste destined for recovery». The Commission operates the system: «The Commission shall operate a central system that allows for the electronic submission and exchange of information and documents referred to in paragraph 1.»

- A shipment-operations lead moves every waste-shipment document flow that still runs on paper to the electronic system before 31 December 2026, and records which clients' loads still use paper today.
- A systems lead checks that the business's booking and tracking tools can show the movement document or the Annex VII information to a carrier and to an inspector during transport, since inspectors may suspend the transport until documents are shown.

*Analytical inference:* the date and the duty to show documents online or in the vehicle are the points where an operational gap becomes a held load; the text states no data format beyond the implementing rules. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the paper period applies to a given load under the Commission's approach.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some wastes sit outside the Regulation: «This Regulation does not apply to: (a) waste, including waste water and residues, generated by the normal operation of ships and offshore platforms» and «(b) waste generated on board vehicles, trains, aeroplanes and ships, until that waste is offloaded for the purposes of recovery or disposal». Domestic carriage is limited: «For transport of waste exclusively within a Member State, only Article 36 shall apply.» Older notified shipments finish under the old rules: «Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 shall also continue to apply to shipments for which a notification has been submitted in accordance with Article 4 of that Regulation and for which the competent authority of destination has given its acknowledgement in accordance with Article 8 of that Regulation before 21 May 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* ship and vehicle waste is outside until it is offloaded; the end of that exclusion is where a forwarder's own load can become a waste shipment. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a shipment started under the old notification still runs under the former regulation.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

An industry body, the recycling trade association EuRIC, stated its view in February 2025: «If no request is submitted by that deadline, a blanket ban on EU exports of recycled materials to those nearly 150 countries will take effect by 21 May 2027». The Commission's page records the position later: «Under the waste shipment regulation, non-OECD countries willing to continue receiving waste from the EU had to submit their request to the Commission by 21 February 2025 .»

*Industry interpretation:* the association's statement is a trade body's view of how the 2027 export rules would work and is not law; the Commission's text and page above are the authority. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any country a client ships to has submitted a request and is on the first list.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers one European Union directive that changes dates and nothing else: «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2025/794 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 14 April 2025 amending Directives (EU) 2022/2464 and (EU) 2024/1760 as regards the dates from which Member States are to apply certain corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements». Its reach is stated in one line: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» The two directives it amends are the reporting and the due diligence rules of the European Union, which a law firm note in the item's material names as «the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)».

What the text states is set out as fact. What it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each question for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. A freight forwarder is not named in the Directive. Commentary from law firms is labelled as commentary, and a date that has passed is written as past.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive does not add a reporting or due diligence duty. It moves the dates from which the duties of the two parent directives apply. The reason it gives is cost: «to avoid the undertakings currently required to report for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025 and on or after 1 January 2026 incurring unnecessary and avoidable costs, the sustainability reporting requirements for those undertakings should be postponed by two years». The aim stays in place: «whilst maintaining the policy objectives of the Green Deal».

For the due diligence directive the reason is time to prepare: «The date from which Member States are to apply Directive (EU) 2024/1760 should be postponed by one year for the first set of companies that fall within the scope of that Directive in order to give companies more time to prepare for the requirements of that Directive». The text adds a practical point: «and to provide them with the opportunity to take into account the guidelines to be issued by the Commission on how they should fulfil their due diligence obligations in a practical manner».

The effective date is set by the text: «This Directive shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». A law firm note gives the dates: «Directive (EU) 2025/794 was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 16 April 2025, entered into force on 17 April 2025, and must be transposed by Member States by 31 December 2025.»

*Analytical inference:* the Directive changes when duties start for companies in the two parent directives and removes none of them, since its two amending articles replace dates only. A freight business meets it as a company that may be in scope, or as a supplier to a company in scope; the Directive itself names neither.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no new duty starts under this Directive, and the date it set for national law has passed. The dates that matter for a freight business are the later reporting years and application dates that it sets, which the sections below give.

- A compliance lead replaces the reporting start dates in the business's compliance calendar with the dates Article 1 sets, «for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027:» and «for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028:», and keeps the old dates only as replaced.
- A compliance lead checks, before the next calendar review, whether the business has more than 3 000 employees and net worldwide turnover above EUR 900 000 000, which sets the due diligence application date, and records the answer for counsel.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Article 1 and Article 2 dates quoted here; the Directive requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which group of companies the business falls into under Articles 1 and 2.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive runs through Member States, not directly to companies: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 December 2025.» They also report back: «They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof.» For companies, the roles named are undertakings, parent undertakings of a large group, issuers and companies formed under the law of a Member State or of a third country.

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder falls in the chain only as a company covered by one of those groups, or as a business partner of one; the Directive names no transport role. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business, or a client that asks it for sustainability information, is a company the Directive's dates cover.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive points to Commission guidelines that are still to come: «the guidelines to be issued by the Commission on how they should fulfil their due diligence obligations in a practical manner». The text gives no date for them.

A wider revision of the two parent directives followed this Directive. The Commission's list records «9 December 2025 Political agreement». A law firm note of January 2026 adds: «On 16 December 2025, the European Parliament approved a provisional agreement reached between MEPs and EU governments on the revised sustainability reporting and due diligence framework.» and «first-reading position which is expected in early 2026». That period has passed and no later status is held, so the agreement is treated here as reported, not as law.

The same note reports that the revision would move the due diligence dates again: «Member States must adopt and publish national implementing measures by 26 July 2028. The measures will apply from 26 July 2029, with the exception of provisions implementing reporting requirements, which will apply for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2030.» It also reports «Member States must designate competent supervisory authorities by July 2028» and «a maximum administrative fine of 3% of a company». On reporting scope it estimates that «These changes take an estimated 80% of companies out of scope compared to the original scope of the CSRD». For smaller suppliers it reports «where they have fewer than 1,000 employees, these companies are considered protected and may decline to provide information requested for reporting».

*Analytical inference:* if the reported agreement becomes law it would replace the 26 July 2027 transposition date and the 2028 application date set by this Directive, and would narrow who is asked for data; this rests on a firm's account of a provisional text, not on a legal act. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the current status of the revision and whether it has been published.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The Directive sets the groups by size and origin. The first due diligence group is «companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), which are formed in accordance with the legislation of the Member State and that had more than 3 000 employees on average and generated a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 900 000 000 in the last financial year preceding 26 July 2028». Third-country companies are covered by a turnover test in the Union: «which are formed in accordance with the legislation of a third country and that generated a net turnover of more than EUR 900 000 000 in the Union». All other companies fall in the last group: «(c) from 26 July 2029 as regards all other companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b), and Article 2(2), points (a) and (b), and companies referred to in Article 2(1), point (c), and Article 2(2), point (c)».

*Analytical inference:* the size and turnover tests decide which date applies to a business; the text sets them for the first group only and leaves the rest to the last group. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which test the business meets and on which financial year the turnover is measured.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Reporting dates. Article 1 replaces dates in Directive (EU) 2022/2464: «(i) in point (b), the introductory wording is replaced by the following: ‘for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027:’ ; (ii) in point (c), the introductory wording is replaced by the following: ‘for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028:’». The recitals describe the schedule that Article 1 replaces, now superseded: «Small and medium-sized undertakings, except micro-undertakings, small and non-complex institutions, captive insurance undertakings and captive reinsurance undertakings are to report in 2027 for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2026.» Article 1 replaces that schedule with the later years above.

Due diligence dates. Article 2 replaces the application dates of Directive (EU) 2024/1760: «Member States shall adopt and publish, by 26 July 2027, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.» The first application date is «(a) from 26 July 2028 as regards companies referred to in Article 2(1), points (a) and (b)». The reporting obligation under Article 16 comes later: «with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029», and for the last group «which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2030».

Transposition. «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 December 2025.»

Scope of the postponement. «The date from which Member States are to apply Directive (EU) 2024/1760 should be postponed by one year for the first set of companies that fall within the scope of that Directive» and «Member States would only need to postpone the application dates pursuant to Article 2 of this Directive in the event that they have already transposed Directive (EU) 2024/1760».

Penalty. The Directive states no penalty, fine or sanction of its own and is addressed to the Member States. It sets dates only. A fine of the revised due diligence rules is reported in Section 6 as part of a provisional text, not as law.

*Analytical inference:* the dates above fall on Member States first and on companies through national law; the Directive gives a forwarder no date of its own. No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2 beyond the dates quoted.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which of these dates applies to the business and whether the national law of each Member State where it operates has already been brought into force.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Directive sets no registration. The reporting it moves is the sustainability reporting of the first parent directive, which now starts for the groups described in Article 1 for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027 and 1 January 2028. The Directive asks Member States to inform the Commission: «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* the report that matters to companies is the one that starts at the dates in Article 1; the Directive sets no format or data field for it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract ties a supplier data request to a reporting year that Article 1 has replaced.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive requires no system of its own; it changes the date by which reporting and due diligence systems of the parent directives must be ready. The Article 2 text keeps a later date for the reporting part: «with the exception of the measures necessary to comply with Article 16, which Member States shall apply to those companies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2029».

- A compliance lead resets the build milestone of any reporting or due diligence data system to the Article 1 and Article 2 dates and keeps the work plan, because the Directive postpones the requirements and does not remove them.

*Analytical inference:* the later dates give time, and the recital gives the reason as more time to prepare; the Directive states no relief from the content of the requirements. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any client has asked for data under the earlier dates and whether that request still stands.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The recital defines the third wave of reporting companies, and the words «except micro-undertakings, small and non-complex institutions, captive insurance undertakings and captive reinsurance undertakings» set who is in that wave; they are not an exemption from this Directive. The first set of reporting companies is not postponed; the recital describes them as «Large undertakings that are public-interest entities with more than 500 employees on average during the financial year» who «are to report in 2025 for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2024».

*Analytical inference:* the Directive changes the dates of the companies named in Article 1 and Article 2, and the first reporting set keeps its original date. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business or a client belongs to the first reporting set.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers the European Union regulation that bans products made with forced labour from the Union market: «REGULATION (EU) 2024/3015 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 November 2024 on prohibiting products made with forced labour on the Union market and amending Directive (EU) 2019/1937». Its reach is set by two lines: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» and «This Regulation lays down rules prohibiting economic operators from placing and making available on the Union market or exporting from the Union market products made with forced labour in order to improve the functioning of the internal market, while contributing to the fight against forced labour.»

What the text states is set out as fact. What it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each question for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. A freight forwarder is not named in the Regulation, and a date that has passed is written as past.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The core rule is one sentence: «Economic operators shall not place or make available on the Union market products that are made with forced labour, nor shall they export such products.» A product counts when forced labour touched any stage: «means a product for which forced labour has been used in whole or in part at any stage of its extraction, harvest, production or manufacture, including in the working or processing related to a product at any stage of its supply chain». It covers every sector: «The prohibition of products made with forced labour should apply to all products, of any type, including their components, and should apply to products regardless of the sector, the origin, whether they are domestic or imported, or placed or made available on the Union market or exported.»

The Regulation sets out what it does not do: «This Regulation does not create additional due diligence obligations for economic operators other than those already provided for in Union or national law.» It also leaves one activity outside: «This Regulation does not apply to the provision of transport services.»

The effective date is split. «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». «It shall apply from 14 December 2027.» Some articles apply earlier: «However, Articles 5(3), 7, 8, 9(2), 11, 33, 35 and 37(3) shall apply from 13 December 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the freight link is customs. The Regulation excludes transport services from its rules, but it lets customs act on the cargo itself, as Sections 8 and 11 set out; so a forwarder that handles import or export declarations meets the Regulation through the product, not through the transport service.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the ban applies from 14 December 2027, about thirteen months away, and no step on a freight business is due within 30 days. The nearest date in the text is for Member States, which «shall, by 14 December 2026, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures», the rules on penalties. The Commission was to publish guidelines and a database by 14 June 2026; that date has passed and no record of either is held.

- A customs-desk lead lists, before the next quarterly review, each client agreement under which the business lodges import or export declarations, because «they shall suspend the release of that product for free circulation or export» is the step customs takes when a product matches a decision.
- A customs-desk lead writes the instruction for a suspended shipment: record the date of the suspension and the product description, since release follows «within 4 working days of the suspension, if the competent authorities have not requested the customs authorities to maintain the suspension».

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the customs articles quoted in Section 8; the text states no cost of a hold, such as storage, and no charge to a client, so those are gaps. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that lodges a declaration for a client is an economic operator or the person who provides product information to customs.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names these roles. The economic operator: «means any natural or legal person or association of persons placing or making available products on the Union market or exporting products». The importer and exporter are defined inside that group. The deciding body is the lead competent authority, «namely a Member State competent authority or the Commission». Customs authorities act on its decisions: «Customs authorities shall rely on the decisions communicated pursuant to paragraph 3 of this Article to identify products that may not comply with the prohibition laid down in Article 3 of this Regulation.» Online sales are inside: «Products offered for sale online or through other means of distance sales shall be deemed to be made available on the market if the offer is targeted at end users in the Union.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight forwarder appears in none of these definitions; the transport exclusion keeps the carriage itself outside, while the customs articles reach the product at the border. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business in any shipment is an importer, exporter or other economic operator, or only the carrier of the goods.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission has guidance and tools to deliver: «The Commission, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, shall make available, by 14 June 2026, and regularly update, guidelines» and, for the risk database, «made publicly available, in all official languages of the institutions of the Union, by 14 June 2026». That date has passed and the capture holds no record that either was published. The guidelines include one for customs: «guidance for customs authorities and economic operators on the practical implementation of Article 27».

Member States have two steps: «No later than 14 December 2025, Member States shall, through the information and communication system referred to in Article 7(1), provide the Commission and the other Member States with the following information», which is past, and the penalty rules: «Member States shall, by 14 December 2026, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures».

The customs product list is still to be set by a delegated act: «The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 33 to supplement this Regulation by identifying the products or product groups for which the information referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article shall be provided to customs authorities.» The power runs «from 13 December 2024». The customs link is a system step: «That interconnection shall start operating no later than 2 years from the date of the adoption of the implementing act», and no adoption date is held. The Commission reviews the rules: «By 14 December 2029 and every 5 years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of the enforcement and the implementation of this Regulation.»

*Analytical inference:* the delegated act and the implementing acts decide which products customs asks information about and how; until they are adopted the customs data a forwarder must provide is not fixed. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the guidelines and the delegated act have been published since the capture.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Three definitions decide whether the Regulation touches a shipment. The first is the product: «means a product for which forced labour has been used in whole or in part at any stage of its extraction, harvest, production or manufacture, including in the working or processing related to a product at any stage of its supply chain». The second is the operator: «means any natural or legal person or association of persons placing or making available products on the Union market or exporting products». The third is what starts action: «means a reasonable indication based on objective, factual and verifiable information for the Commission or competent authorities to suspect that it is likely that a product was made with forced labour».

*Analytical inference:* the product test reaches back through the supply chain, while the operator test is about who places or exports the product. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder arranging carriage and customs clearance for a client is an economic operator under the second definition.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Prohibition. «Economic operators shall not place or make available on the Union market products that are made with forced labour, nor shall they export such products.» Scope limit: «This Regulation does not apply to the provision of transport services.»

Decisions. After an investigation the lead competent authority «shall endeavour to adopt the decision referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article or close the investigation within 9 months from the date it initiated the investigation». The decision includes «an order requiring the economic operators that have been subject to the investigation to withdraw the products that have already been placed or made available on the Union market» and time limits: «reasonable time limits for the economic operators to comply with the orders, which shall not be less than 30 working days; in the case of perishable goods, animals and plants, the time limit shall not be less than 10 working days». A derogation exists: «in order to prevent disruptions to a supply chain of strategic or critical importance for the Union, the lead competent authority may refrain from imposing an order to dispose of the product concerned».

Customs. «The lead competent authority shall, without delay, communicate to the customs authorities of Member States decisions referred to in Article 20 to prohibit the placing or making available of products on the Union market and their export.» Then «Where customs authorities identify, through their relevant risk management system, that a product entering or leaving the Union market might, according to a decision communicated pursuant to Article 26(3), be in violation of Article 3, they shall suspend the release of that product for free circulation or export.» Release comes back on conditions: «that product shall be released for free circulation or exported where all the other requirements and formalities relating to such a release or export have been fulfilled and where either of the following conditions is satisfied: (a) within 4 working days of the suspension, if the competent authorities have not requested the customs authorities to maintain the suspension; in case of perishable products, animals and plants that time limit shall be 2 working days». If the authorities conclude the product was made with forced labour: «they shall require customs authorities not to release it for free circulation or to allow its export» and «customs authorities shall dispose of that product in accordance with national law in compliance with Union law».

Penalties. «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to economic operators for non-compliance with a decision referred to in Article 20». The text adds: «The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» Disposal is paid by the operator: «the disposal of withdrawn products and products remaining with the economic operator in accordance with Article 25, at the expense of that economic operator».

*Analytical inference:* for a shipment, the chain in the text is: a decision is communicated, customs risk management flags a product, release is suspended, and release follows within the stated working days unless competent authorities ask to keep the suspension. The text states no storage, demurrage or delay cost and no charge to a client, so the cost of a hold is a gap.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these customs steps puts a duty, a cost or a liability on a forwarder that lodges the declaration.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation sets no registration for companies. Reporting runs to authorities and customs: «The person intending to place a product, covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article, under the customs procedures» for release or export «shall provide or make available to customs authorities information identifying the product, information about the manufacturer or the producer and information about the product suppliers».

*Analytical inference:* the duty is tied to a delegated act that names product groups, so it applies to a product only after that act exists. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business or its client is the person who provides this information.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text puts a system duty on authorities first, and on the person lodging a declaration for the products a delegated act lists. Decisions are entered where customs can see them: «Decisions communicated pursuant to Article 26(3) shall be entered in the relevant customs risk management environment.»

- A customs-desk lead prepares, once a delegated act names a product group, to add to the declaration process the product identity, the manufacturer or producer and the product suppliers for each line in that group.

*Analytical inference:* the data items above are those the text lists; the format and the product groups are not set until the delegated and implementing acts exist. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the person who must provide this information is the business or its client when the business lodges the declaration.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Several limits are stated. The Regulation does not reach goods already with users: «This Regulation does not cover the withdrawal of products which have reached end users in the Union market.» It sets no new due diligence duty beyond other law, as Section 2 shows. A release is not a clearance of the goods: «The release for free circulation or export pursuant to paragraph 1 shall not be deemed proof of compliance with Union law and, in particular, with this Regulation.» Perishable goods have shorter periods in Section 8.

*Analytical inference:* a release after a suspension does not close the question for the goods, since the text keeps the product open to a later decision. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a released shipment can later be the subject of a decision.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 July 2023 concerning batteries and waste batteries, amending Directive 2008/98/EC and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and repealing Directive 2006/66/EC», the EU Battery Regulation. Its subject is stated at the start of the text: «This Regulation lays down requirements on sustainability, safety, labelling, marking and information to allow the placing on the market or putting into service of batteries within the Union.» Its reach in the Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The text is read as captured.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation covers every kind of battery: «This Regulation applies to all categories of batteries, namely portable batteries, starting, lighting and ignition batteries (SLI batteries), light means of transport batteries (LMT batteries), electric vehicle batteries and industrial batteries, regardless of their shape, volume, weight, design, material composition, chemistry, use or purpose.» It also reaches batteries inside other goods: «It shall also apply to batteries that are incorporated into or added to products or that are specifically designed to be incorporated into or added to products.» The Commission's batteries page gives the start: «On 17 August 2023, the new Batteries Regulation entered into force».

Who the duties fall on is set by role. The importer: «‘importer’ means any natural or legal person established within the Union who places on the market a battery from a third country». The distributor: «‘distributor’ means any natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or the importer, who makes a battery available on the market». And making available: «‘making available on the market’ means any supply of a battery for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge».

*Analytical inference:* these definitions rest on placing batteries on, or supplying them onto, the Union market. A freight business that only carries or stores a client's batteries is not named in these definitions; the duties reach it where it imports in its own name, supplies batteries onward, or handles them for a client as Articles 41 to 43 describe. The text does not name a forwarder or a carrier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role, if any, applies to a freight business for a given consignment.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the next dated step is on 18 February 2027, and the 2025 duties are already in force. «From 18 February 2027, all batteries shall be marked with a QR code as described in Part C of Annex VI.» Two duties already apply since 18 August 2025: «From 18 August 2025, all batteries shall be marked with the symbol for separate collection of batteries (‘separate collection symbol’) as shown in Part B of Annex VI.» and «From 18 August 2025, economic operators that place batteries on the market or put them into service shall fulfil the due diligence obligations laid down in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article». The text read is the Regulation as captured; later amendments to the 18 August 2025 due diligence date are not among the pages held. The importer check holds a non-conforming battery back: «the importer shall not place that battery on the market until it has been brought into conformity».

- A compliance lead lists, before 18 February 2027, each battery type the business imports in its own name and records, per consignment, the importer check: «Before placing a battery on the market, importers shall verify that: (a) the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation referred to in Annex VIII have been drawn up».
- A contract lead adds to the terms with shippers of batteries a clause that names who holds the importer role and who answers for this duty: «Importers shall ensure that, while a battery is under their responsibility, storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise its compliance with Articles 6 to 10 and Articles 12, 13 and 14.»
- A warehouse lead checks the way the business packs and dispatches batteries for clients against «Fulfilment service providers shall ensure that, for batteries that they handle, the conditions during warehousing, packaging, addressing or dispatching, do not jeopardise the batteries’ compliance with Articles 6 to 10 and Articles 12, 13 and 14.»

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the importer duty, the storage and transport duty and the fulfilment duty quoted above, each of which falls on the named operator and not on a carrier as such. A shipment that lacks the marking is exposed to those checks; the text states no cost figure for it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business holds the importer role for any battery it brings into the Union.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation lists its operators: «‘economic operator’ means the manufacturer, the authorised representative, the importer, the distributor or the fulfilment service provider or any other natural or legal person who is subject to obligations in relation to the manufacture, preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing of batteries, the making available or the placing of batteries on the market, including online, or the putting of batteries into service in accordance with this Regulation». A role can shift: «An importer or distributor shall be considered a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of a manufacturer under Article 38, where any of the following applies: (a) a battery is placed on the market or put into service under that importer’s or distributor’s own name or trademark». The distributor has a duty on the register: «the producer is registered in the register of producers referred to in Article 55». The recitals say whom market surveillance authorities can address: «or the importer when the manufacturer is not established in the Union, or an authorised representative mandated by the manufacturer for this purpose, or a fulfilment service provider established in the Union for batteries handled by it when no other economic operator is established in the Union».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits in the chain as importer when it brings batteries in from a third country in its own name, as distributor when it supplies them onward, and as fulfilment service provider when it warehouses, packs or dispatches batteries for a client; in each role the duty is the one the quoted article sets for that role. The text does not define a fulfilment service provider in the passages read. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether warehousing, packing and dispatch services for a client's batteries make the business a fulfilment service provider, and which party is the importer for a consignment the business books.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Commission's batteries page lists guidance and acts that follow the Regulation. On waste batteries: «On July 4 2025, the Commission published new rules for waste batteries that will calculate and verify the rates of recycling efficiency and recovery of materials.» The page names the act: «Commission Delegated Regulation - EU - 2025/606 - establishing the methodology for calculation and verification of rates for recycling efficiency and recovery of materials from waste batteries, and the format for the documentation», and gives its date: «24 July 2025 New rules for calculating and verifying rates of recycling efficiency enter into force». On product design: «Article 11(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 establishes derogations from the removability and replaceability requirements for portable batteries incorporated in products.» The page adds a notice: «The Commission Notice C/2025/214 on 8 January 2025 announced the regular publication of calls for application pursuant to the Commission’s empowerment in Article 11(4) to grant further derogations.» and that «Applicants interested in the granting of further derogations were invited to do so before 30 April 2025.» The page also lists «Commission amending Decision 2000/532/EC as regards an update of the list of waste in relation to battery-related waste».

*Analytical inference:* the guidance and acts on this page concern recycling rates, waste lists and the design of portable batteries inside products; none of the passages read states a rule for carrying or storing batteries. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the waste-list update changes how a shipment of waste batteries is described for a business that arranges such a shipment.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets Commission steps with dates, some already passed. The captured pages do not say whether the acts due on those dates were adopted, so the status of each passed step is not stated here.

- Passed: «By 18 February 2026, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 89 to supplement this Regulation by establishing minimum values for the electrochemical performance and durability parameters».
- Passed: «By 18 August 2026, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 89 to supplement this Regulation by establishing, for the batteries referred to in the first and second subparagraphs, the methodology for the calculation and verification».
- Ahead: «By 18 August 2027, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 89 to supplement this Regulation by establishing mandatory minimum values for the electrochemical performance and durability parameters set out in Annex III for portable batteries of general use, excluding button cells.»
- Ahead: «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall assess the feasibility and potential benefits of establishment of deposit return systems for batteries».
- Ahead: «By 31 December 2030, the Commission shall assess the feasibility of extending the requirements in this Article to portable batteries».
- Ahead: «By 30 June 2031, the Commission shall review and draw up a report on the application of this Regulation».

*Analytical inference:* each step sets values or a review for battery design, recycling or deposit schemes, so it changes the specification a battery has to meet or the scheme a producer joins, not the freight leg; the sections that would update are 8 and 14. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these acts changes the marking or documents that travel with a battery.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question is which category a battery falls in: «For the purposes of Chapter II, where batteries placed on the market can be considered to fall under more than one category, they shall be deemed to fall under the category to which the strictest requirements apply.» The second is when a battery counts as placed on the market: «‘placing on the market’ means the first making available of a battery on the Union market». The third is whether the due diligence chapter reaches a business at all: «This Chapter does not apply to economic operators that had a net turnover of less than EUR 40 million in the financial year preceding the last financial year, and that are not part of a group, consisting of parent and subsidiary undertakings, which, on a consolidated basis, exceeds the limit of EUR 40 million.»

*Analytical inference:* the category rule applies where one battery placed on the market can be considered to fall under more than one category, and the turnover test is applied to the economic operator, not to a client; the text does not say how a shipment of several batteries is categorised. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the category of each battery type the business handles, and whether the turnover exception applies to the business or its group.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Labelling. «From 18 August 2026 or 18 months after the date of entry into force of the implementing act referred to in paragraph 10, whichever is the latest, batteries shall bear a label containing the general information on batteries set out in Part A of Annex VI.» «The separate collection symbol shall cover at least 3 % of the area of the largest side of the battery up to a maximum size of 5 × 5 cm.» «The QR code shall provide access to the following: (a) for LMT batteries, industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2kWh and electric vehicles batteries, the battery passport in accordance with Article 77». «From 18 February 2027 each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service shall have an electronic record (‘battery passport’).»

Economic operators. «Importers shall only place on the market a battery which is compliant with Articles 6 to 10 and Articles 12, 13 and 14.» «Importers shall indicate on the battery their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, their postal address, indicating a single contact point». For distributors: «Where a distributor considers or has reason to believe that a battery is not in conformity with Articles 6 to 10 or Article 12, 13 or 14, the distributor shall not make the battery available on the market until it has been brought into conformity.»

Due diligence. «Economic operators referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall have their battery due diligence policies verified by a notified body in accordance with Article 51». «This Chapter does not apply to economic operators that had a net turnover of less than EUR 40 million in the financial year preceding the last financial year».

Producer responsibility and collection. «Producers shall have extended producer responsibility for batteries that they make available on the market for the first time within the territory of a Member State.» «costs of separate collection of waste batteries and their subsequent transport and treatment». ## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Producers register in each Member State: «Producers shall register in the register referred to in paragraph 1.» «Producers shall only make available batteries, including those incorporated in appliances, light means of transport or other vehicles, on the market of a Member State, if they or, in the case of authorisation, their authorised representatives for extended producer responsibility, are registered in that Member State.» A producer outside the Member State appoints a representative: «A producer as defined in Article 3, point (47)(d) shall appoint an authorised representative for extended producer responsibility in each Member State in which it sells batteries.» Member States name their authorities: «By 18 November 2025, Member States shall notify the Commission of the names and addresses of the competent authorities designated pursuant to paragraph 1.» The reporting format was due from the Commission: «The Commission shall, by 18 August 2025, adopt implementing acts laying down the format for the data and information to be reported to the Commission».

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks operators to keep records and to control handling. For importers: «Importers shall, for 10 years after the battery has been placed on the market, keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of the national authorities». For due diligence: «for 10 years after the last battery manufactured under the relevant battery due diligence policy has been placed on the market». On handling: «Distributors shall ensure that, while a battery is under their responsibility, storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise its compliance with Articles 6 to 10 and Articles 12, 13 and 14.» The QR code is to be printed on the battery: «The labels and the QR code referred to in paragraphs 1 to 6 shall be printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly on the battery.»

*Analytical inference:* a business that imports batteries needs a record system that links each consignment to its declaration of conformity and keeps it for the stated years; a business that stores or dispatches batteries needs a handling procedure that keeps the marking and documents intact. For a business that keeps only a manual shipment file, linking each consignment to its declaration of conformity is a change to make. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is the importer or distributor for each consignment, which decides which of these records it keeps.
